quests.title: Fulminations and Undercurrents

dialogue.t: Hmm? Weren't you in a hurry to go check stuff?
Go on, now... No dawdling!
Checking snack stock... Lower than expected. Please explain, Aino.
Later, later! Can't you see I'm busy... Y'know, saving the poor, anxious inhabitants of this town?
Though the truth has been revealed, our deep connection with the moon remains unchanged — in fact, its power runs in our very veins...
What has changed is our understanding — of where the true moon lies, and that we must walk our own path in life without relying on a power outside of ourselves.
Which is why we now say: Come night or day, may the moonlight connect us.
Ah, guests invited by Nefer, then? Welcome to The Flagship.
The Wild Hunt assault on Starsand Shoal, you mean? Huge wave. First I've ever seen of that size. Good thing it was so brief.
No, no, I mean there's been another, to the north of Nasha Town.
What? How many does that make in the last couple of days now? What are the Lightkeepers playing at...
Can't be helped. There were only a handful stationed on our side in the first place, and the cannon hasn't been fixed yet either. They've been strained to breaking point for a while now, I'll bet.
*sigh* I'm bugging out if this goes on much longer. And here you all told me this was a good place to do business... Fool me once, I say!
Hey now, this could be our big break! My second-eldest brother made his fortune off Wild Hunt attacks, you know. C'mon, let's get moving. There won't be anything left for us if we're late.
Left for us to... scavenge? Mm... I did hear about an overturned cargo vehicle over there...
Hey.
*clears throat*...
Huh... Should've told them that those are dangerous thoughts.

dialogue.sit: Forget it...
I doubt they're the only ones thinking like that.

dialogue.t: Guess you're right. Even if we solved this Wild Hunt problem, they'd probably just jump head-first into some new danger if they thought they could earn some quick Mora...

dialogue.sit: Some self-reflection might not be unwarranted, y'know...

dialogue.t: Hmph... Paimon'll have you know that when it comes to staying outta trouble, greed and cowardice make the perfect match!

dialogue.sit: Should you really be proud of that...
(Still, the Wild Hunt's been getting wilder ever since we foiled that mysterious phantom's plan at Starsand Shoal.)
(The two of them seem closely connected, and that phantom may very well attack again... even though we know almost nothing about it.)
(...In fact, where would we even begin with such an investigation?)

dialogue.t: Hey, look — Aino and Ineffa are here in Nasha Town. Ooh, considering what those people said earlier, d'you think they're here to fix that cannon up?

dialogue.sit: Let's go say hello.

dialogue.t: Hehe, dying to know something, aren't ya? You totally zoned out just now...

dialogue.sit: It's like you can read my mind.
I was wondering if you'd be willing to carry around the Moon Marrow instead...

dialogue.t: Hah! Paimon can even guess what you want for dinner... She'll place the orders tonight, don't you worry!
A—Anyway, let's just go, shall we?
Ah. Familiar faces identified — our good friends, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.
Whoa, free manual labor detected!
Those evaluations could not be more different!

dialogue.sit: Might I ask who this is?

dialogue.t: This is Sousi, Sergeant Major of the nearby Lightkeepers. He's stationed here in this town.
Wait, that means...
He is Flins's superior, as far as position is considered.
A pleasure to meet you all.
This is {NICKNAME} and Paimon, friends of ours. They're experienced adventurers who are new to Nod-Krai.
Hi there!

dialogue.sit: Pleased to meet you. Were you talking about the cannon, by any chance?

dialogue.t: Indeed. The sooner we can get it firing again, the quicker we can ease our current... predicament.
Two more Wild Hunt incursions have come sweeping in at different locations after the last one at Starsand Shoal. Our manpower is already stretched, as it is — this is more than we can handle.
Hasn't Flins gone back to your HQ to ask for reinforcements? When will they arrive?
Huh. Has he now?
Yeah... That's what he said he was gonna do, anyway.
Hmm... He hasn't contacted me about that yet. As per standing orders, he should be leading a team to root out the Wild Hunt, but I haven't received any reports for a while now.
*sigh* Well, he does act outside the remit of his orders sometimes. I'm his superior, yes, but I wouldn't say I have much control over his actions.
So he made the call for backup on his own initiative?
Hard to say. Contacting HQ's a tricky business. I should know, I've tried. They either refuse my requests outright, or end up dragging their feet.

And all the while, we're the ones who have to deal with the Wild Hunt — which, by the way, can strike anywhere in Nod-Krai without warning, sweeping across vast swathes of land. This has been a real test of our endurance, to say the least...
We need to send our personnel where they're needed most. A single missive will not do much to change HQ's attitude, I fear.
Flins understands this well enough, I'm sure.

dialogue.sit: (He sounds nice enough, but it feels like he's hiding something. This whole spiel sounds like a smokescreen.)

dialogue.t: We usually sort our foes ahead of time into ones that our Ratniki will take care of, and ones that we'll target using the cannon.
I've finished the preliminary dispatch work already, but this cannon...
Okay, okay, okay! "Hurry up, Aino." "Fix this, Aino." You fix it if you're in such a hurry! That, or bring me some snacks. This is tiring work over here!
Ugh... Could you at least tell me how long we'll be delayed? We're way past our scheduled firing time.
Well that's your fault for firing too often recently! Machines get overworked too, you know? You could try thinking about their feelings for once, maybe?
Sorry, what? A machine's... feelings?
In layman's terms, this refers to wear and tear. As such, a machine is more liable to fail the "unhappier" it becomes. The exact probability here would be...

Alright, alright. I'm not good at this stuff, I know that. But let me stress that we Lightkeepers are the primary financial backer of this cannon — and our backing does cover the fees for subsequent repair and maintenance.
Hmph. And I'd say that was a good deal for you! You should thank the Krumkake Craftshop — that means me, by the way — for making you such a huge and powerful weapon for such a measly price!
Do you even know how much it would've cost you if you'd bought all the parts legit and fresh off the assembly line?
Reminder: Your future snack budget will have to be halved without the long-term commission payment, Aino. Calculating: A viable and cheaper option... Lavender Melon Candy.
What? No! Absolutely not! I... L—Let me think, alright? It should take, maybe... three more hours?
Wouldn't this place be crawling with more monsters than there are Fungi in Sumeru by then!?

That might not be the concern you think it is. The monsters of the Wild Hunt are only active in the immediate vicinity of its attacks. They will not spread any further... on their own initiative, at least.
We Lightkeepers will also keep an eye on those areas, both to monitor the monsters and to prevent people from entering the cannon's blast radius.
That said... I'm afraid I can't wait three hours before dispatching manpower to the locations that the cannon won't be firing on.
And here's where my need for "manual labor" comes in. There are some checks I haven't finished yet, but with your help, I can get the repairs done sooner.
Wait, but we don't know a thing about this stuff. How much help will we be?
You'll be fine, trust me! Just take this — oh, and this.
Whoa, uh, this book is... so heavy... and what is this?
You can use this Beep-Boopitta to run diagnostics on the cannon. It'll tell you what to do. Oh, and this book will help you understand Beep-Boopitta.
This cannon was built using more than 50 components from different factories and manufacturers. Aino has bound the manuals into one volume. Also, please note: the device's name is "Birgitta."
S—So it's manuals all the way down, huh...
Yup. And if you're quick about this, we might just cut our time-to-fire down by a whole two thirds.

dialogue.sit: We'll do what we can.

dialogue.t: I'll go with you.
Nice! So, you'll check the outside, and Ineffa, inside. Come find me in the control room once you're done. Cool? Cool.
Instructions received. Please go about your work seriously as well, Aino. No snacking while I am away.
Hey! A little snacking will also improve my efficiency by two thirds!
Aino's explanations for things that don't interest her are a bit... "meh," aren't they? Or is that just how geniuses are?
Isn't Beep-Boopitta just following us around? Sure doesn't seem as smart as she said it is. How are we even supposed to know what to check?

dialogue.sit: We might not be at the right spot yet...
There's probably some condition we haven't triggered.

dialogue.t: I've watched Ineffa perform routine repairs before. It seems some sort of maintenance port must first be found, and then this small robot will automatically interface with it.
Ah, so you're in the know. Nice! What does that port look like?
Now that I'm not so sure of. Let's search around together and see what the robot reacts to.
Works for Paimon.
Is this it? Hmm, probably not... Or this one? Oh, ew! Stinks of machine oil!

dialogue.sit: Nope, not here, either...

dialogue.t: Hmm, that thing over there looks promising.
Where? Ooh, yeah, it does. Let's try it out.
Whoa! It's flying...! Does that mean we got it right?
So, uh... What do we do now?

dialogue.sit: Lemme give it a try.

dialogue.t: Well, whaddya know? Aino was right. We got this working without understanding a thing Beep-Boopitta said!
Still, it's impressive how you figured things out right away.

dialogue.sit: Benefit of experience, that's all.
I've figured out puzzles a hundred times more complex before.

dialogue.t: Paimon's up next, along with this stupidly heavy book. Let's see... Should be just like checking a dictionary, right?
The matching result for this symbol is... "Check passed. All systems normal." Wait, is that it?
Well, as they say, "no news is good news."
Yeah, guess you're right. Just feels like we did all this stuff for nothing, that's all... On to the next spot, then.
Hehe, Paimon's getting the hang of this now. It's this thing, right?

dialogue.sit: I'll handle it.

dialogue.t: And this time... Huh? Why are you angry? Oh... Huh, looks like its expressions are also prompts of a kind. Which page is that on...
We need to take note of the order in which its eye colors change — purple, red... Hey, slow down! Paimon didn't catch that!
Beep-deep— bee-dee-deep—
Wha... So now we've got musical prompts too? Weren't you only supposed to be a "beep-boop" machine?
Alright, one final stop. This was quite a trip, huh?
Agreed. I must say, you two have a talent for maintenance work. A bit shaky at points, but not bad for your first job...
Heh, good eye! Paimon's the real deal when she deals for real, y'know!
Really, I'd have liked to share the load, but you were really getting into it, and I didn't want to interrupt.
Ugh, couldn't you have mentioned that earlier?

dialogue.sit: Anyway, let's get this all done in one go.

dialogue.t: Beep-boop-dee-deep!

dialogue.sit: What does that mean? Does the book say anything about it?

dialogue.t: Hmm, a pictorial prompt this time... Don't worry, Paimon's just about gotten the hang of which prompts are listed where.
Uh, we gotta take note of the flashing patterns... "1 yellow flash, nothing for 2 seconds, then 2 yellow flashes" means... the components here are overdue for regular maintenance.
"Maintenance is a high-priority task. The device will be rendered inoperable until it is complete. Switch Beep-Boopitta to Input Mode to send out a signal to unlock components."
The description of Input Mode isn't on this page. Ugh, more page-flipping...

dialogue.sit: After more page-flipping, then even more page-flipping, Paimon manages to adjust the little robot as instructed.

dialogue.t: Phew, that was a real struggle... Well, Paimon needs a break now.

dialogue.sit: Good work, Paimon.

dialogue.t: Good work indeed. But it seems this Input Mode requires some additional work to operate.

dialogue.sit: Allow me.

dialogue.section: Ineffa, Aino, Sousi, Voice from Somewhere

dialogue.t: Looks like we're all good. We can remove this thing now.

dialogue.sit: What is it, anyway?

dialogue.t: No clue, frankly. But whatever — I got a feeling we've all given up trying to figure this cannon out.
I'll go get the replacement component. We should be done once we pop it in here.
What do you think? Maintenance work's easier than running errands, wouldn't you say?
Hehe, that's for sure. We're counting on you, Sousi!
Y'know what? Paimon took him for the stony type at first, but he's actually a pretty nice guy.
Let's wait for him here, huh?
Are your tasks complete?
Yep. Sousi's gone to get the replacement component — we'll be done here once we put it on.
Allow me to check against the recorded data... Yes. This component is approaching its replacement deadline.
The cannon will generate immense recoil when fired. If this is not controlled, the firing platform will become misaligned. This part is designed to anchor the cannon and ensure accuracy when aiming.
Huh. So if the cannon isn't fixed in place... will it start spinning around like some kind of massive firework?
A novel analogy... but an apt one. The large-scale damage that might follow would be undesirable by anybody's standards.
This component is currently easily damaged. The materials are not up to par, and there are still some design flaws. But Aino and I are working to improve it.
Estimated waiting time remaining: 7 minutes. Would you like a krumkake?
Yay! Dessert's just the best after a hard day's work!
Certainly. It will be ready shortly.
*ding*
Observation: Freshly-baked krumkake results in the most efficient improvements upon human happiness indices. As such, I activated an internal heater before starting repairs.
Hehe, thanks for the treat! Aino's lucky to have you.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for the food.
Sure enough, Sousi returns seven minutes later on the dot. You finish installing the spare part before returning to the control room.

dialogue.t: Thanks! Things went great over here too. So, as we agreed, I'll have the cannon up and firing in no time!
Understood. I will inform the inhabitants of Nasha Town and have them make preparations for the shock and noise that will inevitably ensue.
And I will inform the Ratniki stationed around Wild Hunt anomalies to make sure they fall back in a timely fashion.
Thanks for your kind assistance. I'd better make a move — Ratniki from other sites should have sent reports back here, and I'll need to sort them out promptly.
Righty then. Seeya!
Bet this huge cannon's a real sight when it fires.
That is correct. A huge crowd tends to gather on its own accord on such occasions.
Pure, bright energy rays have never failed to inspire obsessed admirers. If you are interested, you can come back later to behold it in all of its glory.
Sure. We did help fix it, after all, {NICKNAME}. It'd be weird if we didn't want to see it in action.

dialogue.sit: A reasonable thought. But before that...
I'd like to investigate the Wild Hunt first.

dialogue.t: Oh, yeah. Wonder where that strange phantom went, never mind what it's doing...
Let's try our luck at The Flagship. See you later, guys!
Heheh! Just be sure not to miss my masterpiece in action!
Is it just Paimon, or are there more people here now? Just as well, since we're sniffing for intel and all...

dialogue.sit: Might as well go in and ask around.

dialogue.t: And maybe — just maybe — let's get some of their Berries and Fried Meat too, huh? We still haven't had it yet!

dialogue.sit: Ah, now you show your true motives.

dialogue.t: Aw, c'mon... Why so uptight?
Excuse me, are you guests? Ah, if you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.
Uh, no, we're not heading back to our room. Are we not allowed in here right now?
That is correct. Only those invited to the Banquet may enter. Our goal is to ensure that our regulars can enjoy peace of mind and comfort, so that they can speak freely with one another.

dialogue.sit: How does one get invited, then?
Name your price.

dialogue.t: Haha. Familiar with our ways already, I see.
But here in Nod-Krai, "channels" hold equal value to Mora. I am but a lowly employee, so you'll have to forgive my inability to help in this matter.
It's fine. Can't be easy being you.
Hmm... Looks like we'll have to switch "channels," then...

dialogue.sit: And I know just the person.

dialogue.t: Nefer, right? The Curatorium does seem to already have an amazing intel network up and running.
B—But if we ask her straight up, she'll likely squeeze us for all we're worth...

dialogue.sit: Good point.
Let's not be quite so forward then.

dialogue.t: Ooh, Paimon's got a plan! Lauma got Nefer to help her prep some medicine, right?
We'll be heading to Hiisi Island later anyway to ask Lauma to help us use the Moon Marrow... Couldn't we deliver the medicine while we're at it?
If Nefer doesn't mention a payment, we can cash our services in as a favor. If she does... then we can use it to haggle!

dialogue.sit: A cunning plan if ever I heard one.

dialogue.t: Hehe, the thought of Mora made it worth the effort of thinking up, hehe... C'mon, let's go!
Apologies. If you wish to return to your room while the Banquet is on, please use the side door.
Hey Black Cat, we're here— Oh, it's you this time.
Hello, you two. What's up?
Not much, just here to say hi! Also, we'll be going to Hiisi Island later... so we can deliver the medicine to Lauma for you, if you need?
(How "thoughtful" of them... Bet they want something from me in return.)
Well... The faster the delivery, the better, naturally. And we're lacking free hands right now, so that would be a great help.
Jahoda's gone to get the medicine, and she should be back any moment now. If you have nothing else to do, feel free to wait here — I'll have someone bring you some snacks.
Don't mind if we do, then. Thanks!

dialogue.sit: You all seem busy. What's the occasion?
Let me guess... the Wild Hunt?

dialogue.t: Oh yes, I'm sure you've all heard about what's going on. Nasha Town's in turmoil, and right now, everyone wants intel — whether it's to strike it rich, save their lives, or escape whatever predicament they've found themselves in.
Ah, so you're busy making Mora. How nice...
It's not all good news, I'm afraid. We're stretched so thin that our clients have taken to competing for our services via "auction."
The price for taking priority slots has all but skyrocketed... In other words, we've had to suspend "free" intel handouts for now.
(She...! Ugh, she cornered us right away. Did she guess what we really wanted from the start?)

dialogue.sit: Is there anything we can do for you, then?

dialogue.t: *sigh* If there's anything that worries me right now, it's the Wild Hunt. It affects everything we do, yet the number of people who can ensure "cargo safety" in the face of such a threat is vanishingly small.
Hmm? That doesn't sound too hard. If you need something delivered, hit us up and consider it sent!
Is that so? But... Ah, no, no, forget I said anything. I mean, you're great heroes. How could I waste your precious time on trifles like these?

dialogue.sit: As a matter of fact...
There is something we'd like to know...

dialogue.t: Is there, now? You should've said so sooner! Far be it for me to extort you, of all people, for intel... But seeing as you so kindly made me an offer, I suppose I'll accept.
(Agh! What's there left for us to say here...!?)

dialogue.sit: On account of our previous cooperation?

dialogue.t: More like... our common perspective.
Most who live here only wish to defend their own interests — but we are different, are we not? We both seek to resolve the chaos that the Wild Hunt has caused.
(Hmph... More like "make a profit off the Wild Hunt"! Paimon doesn't believe a word she says!)
Dissatisfied, are we?
The number of commissions over at the Adventurers' Guild spikes during tumultuous times too. Would you call taking those jobs for Mora a sin?
Well, uh... That's...
We might squeeze some advantage out of chaos, but equally, chaos could uproot everything we've built at any time. Such is the threat of the Wild Hunt today.
And what business would there be left, should it end in some great slaughter, or put to flight many who call Nasha Town their home?
And as I understand, the two of you are here in Nod-Krai to follow a trail of clues yourselves, no?
Well, yeah...
In that case, we should keep Nod-Krai the "paradise" people say it is. At least, until our respective goals have been accomplished.
You must understand. No force exists here that would inspire unconditional unity amongst all parties.

dialogue.sit: I do get it...
But I'm not doing this just for me.

dialogue.t: After that incident with Lauma, I'm inclined to believe you. Your selflessness is admirable, to be sure, and rare around these parts.
(Though it's rare for a reason, kid...)
Just a shame that our mysterious phantom has hidden itself well. Between that and its ability to shift shapes, it will no doubt be a most slippery customer.
Really, I'd be all too glad to pass on any additional intel I gain. We make a good team after all, don't you think? You front and center, me behind the curtain.
That... does make sense. Sorry, Nefer. Paimon took you for someone who only cares about profit.
A well-placed "only" indeed, Paimon. Nothing is wholly divorced from profit of some kind.
Wait. So you were ready to work with us from the start?
Why, of course. In fact, I was wondering when I might bring this up the moment you entered.
B—But...!
Hey Boss, I'm back—! Huh? You guys are here too?
Indeed they are. In fact, they've volunteered to deliver the medicine to Lauma on our behalf, and totally free of charge. Such kind souls, aren't they?
Really? Great! In that case, guess I'll be clocking out now—
Ah, ah, ah... Got a few more places for you to visit right here, dear.
(Huh? Haven't I already worked a few days' worth of overtime already...? Eh, well, guess the extra Mora's pretty nice...)
Well, we'd better get this medicine delivered, pronto.

dialogue.sit: Wait a sec... Is this salt?

dialogue.t: Huh? Surely not? The special medication from before wasn't salt, was it?
Wait, that can't be! Let me see... Agh! This... This isn't right. How could it be salt!?
*sigh*...
Ugh, it was raining back there, so... Could it have happened while I was resting in the store...!?
Sorry! Sorry, Boss! I'll get it back right now. Trust me, I'm super fast!
Hey, hey! Slow down, you might get hurt!
Well, then. Any plans? If not, what say we go into town and ask around about the Wild Hunt?
We were thinking of doing that, but we didn't get much out of it... The townspeople are a bit wary of us, and we can't get into The Flagship right now...
Ah, yes. The Banquet is on today. Perfect timing — that's where we'll go.
Huh? Can you get us an invitation?
Oh, come now. What are we, sticklers for the rules?
Lady Nefer, a pleasure to see you. Oh? And our guests from earlier, I see.
That's right. My apologies, consider it my fault for not having explained the Banquet's rules to them beforehand.
Oh, no, it was no trouble at all. Please, do come in.
Uh... Yeah, sure. Thanks.
(Not even an invitation check? Paimon didn't realize Nefer was such a big shot... Guess "channels" really do take you places.)

dialogue.sit: After you enter, Nefer brings you and Paimon to a spot near the bar before walking into an inner room to talk business with The Flagship's manager.
As you wait, you notice that everyone seems wary of the two of you, and the volume of the chatter lowers significantly.
This stifling atmosphere persists until Nefer returns...

dialogue.t: Finally! Now, what do we—
Pardon me. I'm sure we're all having a good time, but I would like you all to meet a mysterious guest I invited for just this occasion.
I give you tonight's special guest, a renowned mixologist from Mondstadt!
A—Are you serious!?

dialogue.sit: Ladies and gentlemen, it is an honor.

dialogue.t: N—Nice to meet you all...
I'm sure that no more needs to be said about Mondstadt's wine industry — after all, we are all connoisseurs of fine drink here.
The special drinks menu is being set before you as we speak. Now then, for a time, let us set aside our worries and enjoy these exotic spirits from afar.
Ah, I see. A new face for the bar.
And here I was thinkin', "that ain't a familiar face." No wonder...
Well, it's a rare occasion to be sure. Wanna order a glass or two?
Hmm, sounds intriguing...
I spoke to the owner. The bar is all yours.
The recipes are available for your perusal here. Not to worry, I've taken the liberty of removing the more... challenging options.

dialogue.sit: I guess we'll just have to give this a shot.
Previous experience coming in handy. Who'd have thought it...

dialogue.t: How'd you set this all up so quickly?
Well, as long as you know what both sides need, negotiations are essentially just a process of confirming the deal. No one would turn a beneficial offer down now, would they?
The Flagship already had plans to invite a professional mixologist from Mondstadt anyway — so consider this a trial run, with the list of drinks brought out in advance.
Demyan will assist you. Serving guests with drinks will be the perfect opportunity for you.
Of course, every guest will have their quirks, so you'll have to be careful not to arouse their suspicions.
Got it. We'll give it a try.
In the meantime, I'll go mingle with some of the guests who... pique my interest. There'll be a little event during the Banquet's second half, by the way. See you then.
Hello. How may I assist?

dialogue.sit: Make Drinks
Leave
Make Drinks
Make Drinks

dialogue.t: W—Wait. What are you angling for, exactly?
Oh, so this order was yours, huh?
Indeed. So, any notable news?

dialogue.sit: Not for the moment.

dialogue.t: Ah, you two must be Nefer's friends. A pleasure to meet you. If you've got a moment, let's have a drink — on my tab, of course.
Paimon doesn't recall there being any other orders right now. Sure then, we can take a break.
Haha. Then come, sit! Demyan, two Wildberry Trails, if you would — without alcohol. Much obliged!
Hintsa's the name. I help out at the Rossum Workshop in town — they usually put me in charge of making and repairing simple machines.
Paimon's name is Paimon. Pleased to meet'cha!

dialogue.sit: I'm {NICKNAME}.
They call me the Honorary Cocktail Knight.

dialogue.t: ...Anyway, help me keep an eye out, alright? Valuable intel will be suitably compensated.
Oh, come on, is that how it is between us? I mean, I wouldn't even have this job if it hadn't been for your help back then.
So you've known each other a long time?
That's right. I came to Nod-Krai with nothing at all. Would've starved on the streets if I hadn't met Nefer.
She lent me money to study a craft, and even introduced me to Aino and the Voynich Guild, which is how I slowly carved out a living for myself.
That's... Yeah, that's a huge favor.
Huh, so Nefer can be a nice person sometimes huh?
Haha! Well, I'd also say she needed a willing and able machinist at her disposal.

dialogue.sit: Wait, don't we already have Aino for that?

dialogue.t: Come now, Aino's talents are better spent on issues bigger than basic machine repair and component manufacture.
I did think myself a dab hand at such work at first, but compared to her, I might as well be a trainee who couldn't weld a wire to save his life. Got the scoldings to show for it, too.
It took me a long while, but I finally got to the point where I could make my own machines and even maintain some of Aino's relatively complex ones, like kuuvahki detectors or mechanical arms.
He's the one responsible for maintaining Jahoda's robotic arm.
Ooh, speaking of that, didn't Sousi have a mechanical arm too?
That's right, one of Aino's masterful designs. I could never design one of those in my life, but if you gave me its blueprint, I could hammer one out.
Nowadays, I've got regular customers, which makes for a decent keep. Even got a kid, if you can believe it — I wouldn't have, had you told me my future when I first arrived here.
On the flipside, being a family man means I can't just flee this place whenever I feel like it... so I'm afraid I'm counting on you to help solve this Wild Hunt crisis.
All the more reason to be proactive and do your part. Wringing our hands in despair does us no good in times of crisis.
Oh, wait. Just another question that's been bothering me. Have you heard anything about people seeing illusions within Wild Hunt anomalies? People they know, perhaps?
Hmm. I have heard of humanoid shapes being sighted, but familiar faces... No.
Most would think they'd lost their wits from fright if they started hallucinating. After all, no ordinary person could survive an assault from those monsters.
Does this have anything to do with our current Wild Hunt crisis?
Perhaps, perhaps not.
Ah, alright, I get it. I'll keep my ear to the ground for you — and naturally, my lips will stay tightly sealed.
Then we'll take our leave. Enjoy your drinks.
He's a social man. You can often find him here chatting with friends, and he's had contact with all manner of clients.
Since he's never heard of the Wild Hunt exhibiting the power to imitate familiar faces, might it be safe to assume that our phantom wants to keep that a secret?
Huh, that does sound worth noting... How about we go talk to a few more people?
A good idea, and one our upcoming activity will facilitate. Let me show you how it's done.
Come, back to the bar.
Thank you for waiting, everyone. The Roulette Showdown is ready to begin.
Finally! Haha.
C'mon, let's go try our hand.
Joining us, new guy(girl)?
Uh, we'll pass...
Haha, no you won't. The one who'll be mixing the Roulette Special has to take part — those are the rules.
Ah, but...

dialogue.sit: (There's Nefer's hand-signal again. Let's go with it.)
Sign me up.

dialogue.t: Haha! That's more like it!
Since we have a new friend with us today, let me go over the rules in brief.
The wheel before you is divided into an inner and outer circle. Participants must take turns to spin the pointer of the inner circle. Whatever beverage it stops at, our lucky contestant will drink.
The drinks are divided into juice, tea, and alcohol, with that last further divided into three levels by intensity.
Spin your way to a non-alcoholic beverage, and you'll score no points. Otherwise, you get 1 to 3 based on alcohol content.
During a round of drinking, one participant may choose another with less points than them, and pose a question, which the other party must then answer.
This sounds like it might favor those who score higher, but push your luck, and you might not recall any answers you were given the next day. Defeats the purpose, wouldn't you say?
And that's why the person mixing the drinks has to take part. Y'know, just in case they decide to pour heavy, then sit back and watch the show.
(Not that our newcomer looks like the drinking type. Either way, looks like we're in for a show.)
Anything you drink will be replenished — and additionally, I have decided to sponsor a "grand prize" for this grand occasion...
...A single serving of "Dark Horse."
What? Do my ears deceive me? A chance to drink "Dark Horse" in Nod-Krai?
"Dark Horse," eh... Guess we'll have to take part now, huh?
Hehe... Indeed, the "Dark Horse" could be yours to enjoy, so long as your luck holds — and so long as you can remember its taste the day after.
And if our lucky winner can drain the whole serving in one go, they will gain the right to ask everyone a question, regardless of their score.
High-risk, high-reward... That's gotta be some strong alcohol.
Now, if there are no other questions, let us begin. Allow me to get the ball rolling.
Intensity 3? Looks like I'll have to put my back into it today.
Let's go!
Wow, this is kinda intense...
My turn, my turn! Alright, man, 'fess up. You've been making a killing lately — where's it all been coming from?
Hey, bro, I heard you met up with some big shot from the Voynich Guild! Mind introducing me sometime?
Tch... A normal drink, huh? Must be my lucky day.
We've reached the final round of the Roulette Showdown. Let's see who gets the last laugh.
Gotta shay, you Mondstadters really know your alrcohol... Those rrecipes are... superr good... teash me, would ya...
Hahah, I wuz wantin' to ask 'bout yer waif... Err, your wife...

dialogue.sit: (I've rolled non-alcoholic drinks without fail the last few rounds. This zero-point game is no accident...)
(Similarly, Nefer's been maintaining an ever-so-slight lead, and has been using it to ask ever-so-slightly probing questions. That can't just be luck.)
(I can tell that Dobrawa was lucky enough to survive stumbling into a Wild Hunt. But Nefer's turn is...)

dialogue.t: You're up.

dialogue.sit: (...Ahhh. She left him to me.)

dialogue.t: Whooooa! Newface here just drew the "Dark Horse"!
Bottoms up! Bottoms up!
H—Hey. Will you be alright, {NICKNAME}? You wanna just give this one to Paimon?
Whoa, he(she) actually downed it in one gulp!
Nice job! No wonder you Mondstadters have such a reputation!

dialogue.sit: What did you see while you were inside the Wild Hunt anomaly?

dialogue.t: Me? Well, what do you think? Monsters, of course!

dialogue.sit: Only monsters?

dialogue.t: Absolutely. If there was something else, I didn't stop to see it. Just took off as fast as I could...
Oh, and guess who showed up just as I'd gotten out of there? Those good-for-nothin' Ratniki, that's who.
If my luck had been just a little worse, they'd have found nothing but my corpse — or whatever was left of it, anyway.
...Either way, there's nothing in there you'd want to see.

dialogue.sit: (Even those who have had a personal encounter with the Wild Hunt know nothing about the strange phantom we saw. It seems Nefer's judgment was on point.)

dialogue.t: I see some downcast faces. Why, have we all hit our limit?
Says who? I'm still raring to go!
Cuz you... din' drink... Dat mush...
Hehe, in that case, let me raise another glass — to a blast of a Showdown, and a wonderful evening.
Hmm? Are they playing cards? Paimon spies some Elemental Dice...
Same as usual, then? One die, 100,000 Mora.
I'm not here to do business with you...
Come now, I've already ordered us drinks. Or are you looking to add another line to your ledger of arrears?
O—Oh, so this is a business deal?
So, let's go over this again. One die, 100,000 Mora.
Hehe, then we have a deal. Come, you two, take a seat as well.
*sigh* What are we even doing here?
I can give you three things: The features of the Wild Hunt, the exact locations where it has appeared, and the intel we've received from the Lightkeepers.
The Wild Hunt is in fact a phenomenon linked to Abyssal power. Fog and monsters follow in its wake, posing a lethal danger to ordinary people.
On the flipside, these monsters cannot leave the fog, so the disaster cannot spread quickly—
We already know all that.
*sigh* Fair enough. Then I won't beat around the bush.
Here's a map of current Wild Hunt anomalies that I snagged from the Lightkeepers, including the locations they'll soon be bombarding.
That's... a lot.
We've never seen anything like this either. That's why everyone's so worked up.
That's not enough. Four dice.
Cool it, alright? I'm not done...
Now, the Lightkeepers don't want you to know this, but weirdly enough, more Wild Hunt sites have disappeared than their involvement would indicate.
Isn't that normal? They're not the only ones fighting the Wild Hunt, after all. Adventurers do that too... and maybe some just go poof by themselves?
I'd agree. And really, we've always had a small, stable discrepancy between reported anti-Wild Hunt ops and anomalies cleared. That variance... has become a gulf lately.
What could that even mean...
I've got two theories. One, that some new force is clearing the Wild Hunt out in secret... or two, that some Ratniki are not reporting the work they do on purpose.
The odds of the former happening is low. Not many organizations can even engage the Wild Hunt, never mind keep those operations a secret.
If you're interested, I'd recommend following the latter train of thought.
Hmm, Paimon doesn't really get it... What would anyone gain from doing that?

dialogue.sit: Let's just note it down first.

dialogue.t: Now that's what I call interesting intel. No wonder you've been doing well for yourself lately — even if you've mostly just been reselling my intel.
Please... stop. This is all I've got for you.
Oh, stop that. Why, people might start thinking me a bully.
Let me give you an opportunity, instead — out of respect for your independent intelligence-gathering. An answer to a simple question, for 50,000 off your debt.
Have you heard of people seeing familiar faces within a Wild Hunt anomaly, or experiencing something akin to, say, an illusion?
No, nothing like that. Nothing at all but ghostly shadows...
Nothing at all, hmm? Not even for 50,000 Mora? Either you don't take your debt seriously, or you're confident you can pay it off...
H—Hey, no means no, alright? This is about my dignity as an intel broker — Mora doesn't factor in here at all.
Okay, well that puts me at ease.
Ugh, you really are the same as ever...
And you've learned quite well. Go on, then. I'll swing by again — sometime soon, perhaps.
So... You're his creditor?
Indeed I am. He's resold my intel quite a few times now, pocketing the difference afterwards. Rather dishonest dealing, if I may say so.

As luck would have it, he would only purchase information from me when he was just about done negotiating with his buyer, so I arranged a little something just for him. A painful lesson, you might call it.
Ergh, that sounds brutal...
Oh, I was downright beneficent in charging for that betrayal. It was more about the message, really.

dialogue.sit: Good thing we're on the same team...

dialogue.t: In any case, I believe that's all we'll get here. Let's go through what we've learned outside.
Most of our intel seems quite dispersed, so let's try piecing it all together.
Well... First, no one else has seen that weird phantom, apart from our encounter on Starsand Shoal.
Indeed. And we have that from multiple accounts, so each statement corroborates the others.
What in Teyvat could that phantom be planning...?

dialogue.sit: The Wild Hunt anomaly that occurred at Starsand Shoal seems quite unique.

dialogue.t: Agreed. Instances of the Wild Hunt afflicting Nod-Krai in general have increased in frequency, but the phenomenon itself hasn't changed much.
What you encountered must have been something special, with our mastermind concealing themselves within... in order to target the Moon Marrow.
In which case, two questions arise: Who is this mastermind? And why would they want the Moon Marrow?

dialogue.sit: (Additionally, that intel broker mentioned that some Lightkeepers might be withholding information. Given the inconsistencies in Flins's words and deeds, he might be a likely suspect...)
(But... let's not share that with Nefer for now.)

dialogue.t: I'll continue investigating along these two lines. We can reconvene again if any progress is m—
I—I—I'm back!
Luckily, the store owner kept the medicine bottle I left on the table safe for me. Here you go!
Thanks a bunch, Jahoda! Take a break, you've earned it.
Oh no, I've got work to do later, and anyway, isn't the cannon about to go off?
I was watching it the whole way back, praying it wouldn't fire — not until I got back, y'know? Again, lucky me.
Huh, so you're interested in that big gun?

Of course! I mean, just think about it. Something that size is bound to be comprised of thousands, even tens of thousands of parts, fused in such a way that it can operate smoothly and fire off a super-giant, super-strong beam!
Isn't that just so cool— I mean, miraculous? Like, a miracle created through countless careful calculations?
Mmm. It has been a while since the last time it fired. Go on, feel free to go watch. Work can wait — for a while.
Ah, thanks, Boss! Anyway, y'all wanna come? It'll be worth the while and worth your wait, I swear!
Eh, might as well. Fruits of our labor and everything, y'know?

dialogue.sit: Let's go.
We're pretty much going that way, anyway.

dialogue.t: Woohoo, let's go! Kaboom!
Wow, what a crowd! People seem pretty excited, too. Just goes to show how big a deal this cannon is, huh?
Oh, for sure! One shot, one kill — problems solved! Simple and practical, just the way we like it.
And even if that wasn't how it worked, just listen to how it roars! If that isn't "power," I don't know what is...
If only I had that kinda strength...
Hey, don't think like that! Your skills and smarts have been a big help to us too!
(R—Really? They think that? Ohh... I'll do my best next time we work together, for sure!)
Hey, look, it's starting!
Whoo!
Nice one!
Finally, all fixed up. Nothing to fear now, hahaha!
Hehe, awesome. Felt that one in my bones!
Whew... That sure was powerful... and pretty dazzling, too! Guess that's why everyone's been counting on this thing. Surely the Wild Hunt doesn't stand a chance!

dialogue.sit: Perhaps we should use it more often.
It would certainly save the Lightkeepers a whole lot of running around.

dialogue.t: Ahhh! I feel so... alive right now! Overtime? Hah. It's gonna be a piece of cake!
Y'know, Paimon's been wondering... If you're so interested in machines, why don't you go work for Aino?
Hehe. That's what we call drawing a line between your work and your hobbies.
I've got some mechanical talents, sure, but this job I have now? No one can do it but me — not even Aino or her silly robots!
Anyway, gotta go. Seeya later—!
Says the person who got salt and medicine mixed up...
Huh... Looks like the crowd's breaking up as well. Let's head over to Hiisi Island — best not keep Lauma waiting.

quests.description: The Wild Hunt has left many secrets behind, and the shadows hidden within the Abyss begin to churn. After chaos strikes, unease spreads amongst people, making them desperate for solutions…

quests.title: The Dark Side of Memory

dialogue.t: Let's see now... What's changed since we were gone?

dialogue.sit: Not as much as I'd imagined.

dialogue.t: Yeah. If anything, looks like things are settling down. That's Lauma for ya!
Hey there, Lauma. We're back!

dialogue.sit: How have things been these past few days?

dialogue.t: The clean up work has been much more complicated than I expected. Solving problems that have built up over time is a tall order, to say the least...
I believe it will take a few weeks more. Fortunately, those who remained appear to have shaken off the initial confusion and are becoming more proactive by the day.
It's as if they've finally been forced to come face-to-face with what their faith actually is.
And it's all thanks to you!
No, I... I should have done this a lot sooner.

I've been focused on taking care of myself these past few days, so I'm in a good place. And since you're looking after the Moon Marrow for us, I should be able to help you investigate the truth of the past.

dialogue.sit: Thanks for remembering.

dialogue.t: Speaking of which, have you heard anything new about that phantom?
I've tried asking around, but to no avail.
What about you?
We haven't made much progress either, but here's what we've got...
I think I've got the gist of it... Sounds like you've got your work cut out for you too. Don't forget to take good care of yourselves.
In any case, come this way, {NICKNAME}.
What do you see?

dialogue.sit: (This is... Nod-Krai? This all looks familiar...)
(Is that... a shooting star in the sky?)
(No, wait! That's our spaceship!)

dialogue.t: Is it over already?
This appears to have occurred a long, long time ago. The memories I sensed are highly turbulent and disordered, so that is all my power allows me to discern.

dialogue.sit: (At least we now know where our spaceship landed in Nod-Krai... Near Starsand Shoal, or so it seems.)
(That matches with what Lumine(Aether) told me... But I want to know more...)

dialogue.t: Huh? What's the matter?
The flowers changed color...

dialogue.sit: (These flowers are a reflection of The Damselette's powers. Does that mean she's...)
(I remember her mentioning that she wanted to use the Moon Marrow to restore some of her power...)
Paimon...

dialogue.t: Yeah, we should go see her, and see if we can help her in some way.
I'll leave that in your hands, then.
Oh, wait — here you go! This is the medicine you asked the Curatorium of Secrets to help prepare earlier.
Ah. Thanks for coming all this way with it. You've been a huge help.
Also... If I may, I have a feeling that "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar" might be able to help you get a more detailed glimpse at the memories about your spaceship.
Ooh, that's true. She's the Kuutar, after all!
But we'd best check if she's doing okay first.
Seeya later, then!
Oh... She doesn't look so good...
S—Sorry for disturbing you, but are you okay?

dialogue.sit: Has your condition worsened?

dialogue.t: ...Dizzy.
...It's like... I'm returning to the moon.
Wait, it's not that bad, is it!?
Hmm? I... sense the moon's power... within you?

dialogue.sit: We got the Moon Marrow back from the Fatui. Can it help you in any way?

dialogue.t: Mmm... And what do you require this time?
C'mon, don't even think about that. Right now, you gotta focus on getting better!

dialogue.sit: (Has this just become habitual for her, after living in relationships of mutual benefit for so long...?)
I might need your assistance in the future.

dialogue.t: ...Oh. Very well.
Give me your hand.
*exhale* ...Back to earth. My thanks.
Uhh, your feet never left the ground... But anyway, feeling any better?
Significantly.

dialogue.sit: What did you do?
...Or maybe, what did I do?

dialogue.t: The moon within your body... it is as silent as a reflection in the water... Fascinating.
I merely drew forth a ray of its light from the water. Enough to keep me tethered to the ground for now.

dialogue.sit: I think I sensed some other changes as well...

dialogue.t: That is the "Moon Goddess's Favor." All things I come into contact with will bear this mark.
It is harmless, and will fade over time.
Speaking of which, do you wanna be the Moon Marrow's custodian, now that you've got your power back?
It's supposed to be something that belongs to a "god" in any case, right?
It is the remains of Aria, Goddess of the Eternal Moon.
So it does have to do with... Wait, what!?
Did you not know this already?
Lauma just said it was different from the other fragments, and that she could sense divine power within it.
And she is correct. When I drew that ray of moonlight from the Marrow, I also drew some memories from within.
That is how I know that it belongs to the Goddess of the Eternal Moon.
But Lauma also saw the past by using the Moon Marrow. Why didn't she see that...

dialogue.sit: (Lauma mentioned that she could only catch brief, blurry snippets... Perhaps this is something that only a Moon Goddess could sense...)

dialogue.t: There were once three moons in the sky, each belonging to a goddess who ruled over it.
But after the war of funerary flame, all three lay slain, and two of the three moons were shattered during the conflict.
After Aria's death, her power coalesced into this Moon Marrow...
The Iridescent Moon's remains have never been found, and while the Frost Moon's goddess died herself, her moon was never broken.
As the prophecy stated, this moon would birth a new deity sooner or later — the entity the Frostmoon Scions call the "Kuu{RUBY#[S]Moon Maiden}tar."
I can sense that my power belongs to the Frost Moon. But it lies beyond the false sky, too distant from me.
Forget "controlling" it... "Sensing" it alone requires immense effort.
W—Wait, l—let Paimon count this up... We have the Eternal Moon's Marrow with us, no one can find the Iridescent Moon's... Does that mean you have the Frost Moon's Marrow inside you, then?
No. It can only form after the moon goddess is dead. Consider it a form of energy core.
You may as well ask if there are rocks on the moon.
Oh, so you're saying that you represent the Frost Moon's power, right?
Yes. Now, a god with a Gnosis is named an Archon... Since you bear the Moon Marrow, does that make you a "Moon Goddess"?

dialogue.sit: I doubt that's the same thing...

dialogue.t: You do not wish to become one?
That's not really the problem here! Also, why are you so eager to pass that title on to someone else!?
Anyway, never mind this "becoming a Moon Goddess" stuff for now. We're asking if we should return this Moon Marrow to you.
I do not desire it.
Huh?
Nor does it desire to come to me.
And... What does that mean?
When I came into contact with its power, I sensed a kind of... "rejection."
I can only guess that this is because I, too, am a Moon Goddess. Two moons will not rise at the same time, let alone consume one another.

dialogue.sit: Guess it's stuck with me for now, then.

dialogue.t: You sure that's gonna be okay? Lauma did say that you've hidden its power well, but The Damselette sensed it just fine.
And it's the Wild Hunt we're dealing with here, not some run-of-the-mill enemy. If it detects the Marrow...
The Wild Hunt? You speak of that phenomenon as if you were describing a person.
Well, it sure looks like there's a person behind it all — someone with a super clear goal, too. They've been after the Moon Marrow non-stop!
That seems to ring a bell...
Huh? Does it really?
My colleagues used to mention someone, back when I was still with the Fatui.
He hailed from Khaenri'ah, gaining Abyssal power during the Cataclysm... and he had a consuming fixation on the moons...
Khaenri'ah? Well, we don't know if the phantom we saw has anything to do with that, but the details kinda match... What was his name?
I only know what others called him — the "Rächer of Solnari."

dialogue.sit: One of the Five Sinners!?

dialogue.t: Ah... There was that title too, yes.
Eh!? Wait a second... Dain mentioned him, didn't he? D—Does that mean that our enemy is Rerir, one of the Five!?

dialogue.sit: If that was the case, surely he'd be stronger than this, though...

dialogue.t: I have heard that he disappeared not long after the Cataclysm.
But when I asked my colleagues where he went, they replied, "Do you really not know?"
Why would they say that...
The tale of his final fate has it that he fell into the "moon's reflection," from which there can be no return.
Wait, hold up, pause... There's just... too much information!
I felt the same. They seemed to think that I should be the one who would know everything about the moons.
But as I said... My "prologue" lies beyond the false skies. I do not even remember my name...
Oh...
Either way, following his departure, the Wild Hunt situation worsened drastically — and it has since become a byword for Abyssal disaster.
The present phenomenon may have inherited the same title, but it far surpasses its past incarnation in both scale and lethality.
Ugh. To think that we're up against one of the infamous Five Sinners...
That's way too much for us to handle! That incident on Starsand Shoal must've been luck, then... or maybe he wasn't giving it his all?
And even then... He still defeated Marionette...
Oh? What did you just say? Would you mind... repeating that?
Err... That's your... ex-colleague? So... we were on Starsand Shoal together, and she was beaten by the Wild Hunt too...
Did you just... laugh?
(She totally did!)
Are you two on bad terms, or something?
No... I simply imagined the put-out expression she must have worn in that moment, and found it... interesting.
She seemed quite shaken.
Oh, she'll adjust soon enough. She's very good at that.
Okay, anyway... We've gotten off topic. Now that we know how dangerous the guy targeting the Moon Marrow is... You sure you wanna carry it around with you, {NICKNAME}?
If Fatui intelligence is to be believed, Rerir would prevail even if all of Nod-Krai were to stand against him.
Perhaps something restricts him... if only for the moment.

dialogue.sit: Before I decide, there's a favor I'd like to ask you, Columbina.

dialogue.t: What do you need?

dialogue.sit: Do you think you'd be able to show me what happened when my sister(brother) and I arrived in Nod-Krai? I mean, when our spaceship first landed?

dialogue.t: Sure.
That was quick!
As I said — this, to me, is but a single ray of moonlight. Nothing to it.
Give me your hand, and ready yourself.

dialogue.sit: (This is what we saw before, only clearer...)
(It seems we landed safely, at least...)
(A lot of time appears to have passed...)
(We're still inside the spaceship. To think we were in there for so long... When did Lumine(Aether) get out, I wonder?)
(Wait. Is that... Lumine(Aether)!?)
(But, how can that be? No one left the ship from the moment we landed... The door hasn't even been opened yet!)
Where... is this?
Aether(Lumine)! Come on! We have to leave this place!
What?

dialogue.t: H—Hey! Are you okay?

dialogue.sit: Our spaceship... A long, long time passed after we landed...
No one left the ship during that time, but Lumine(Aether)... found me from outside of it, somehow...

dialogue.t: Huh!? How would that even be possible?

dialogue.sit: I don't know...

dialogue.t: The secrets within memories are like cookie crumbs. Take a bite, and they go everywhere.

dialogue.sit: (There's... something seriously strange going on here. I have to get to the bottom of this.)
(But as Nefer said, there'll be nothing to investigate if Nod-Krai is destroyed first...)
Alright. I'll keep the Moon Marrow with me.

dialogue.t: Uhh... Well, if you say so, Paimon can't stop you, but still... oooh...
Will you need my help?

dialogue.sit: Help with...?

dialogue.t: I could help you conceal the Marrow.
You could? That'd be great!
Detecting it within you is already no easy task, but I can teach you to further conceal its presence using kuuvahki.
Like this...
Ooh! Looks like a shield!

dialogue.sit: (This... feels so soft and gentle... just like the moonlight...)

dialogue.t: Can you sense it? Now, try to maintain it.
You learn quickly.
Huh. Looks pretty sturdy. Could probably be used in self-defense in a pinch, huh?

dialogue.sit: Thanks for teaching me that...

dialogue.t: Are you always here, Columbina? It's kinda dangerous out there, sure, but have you, like, taken a walk outside or something?
...Dislike strangers.

dialogue.sit: And where do we rate on that scale?

dialogue.t: Slightly better.

dialogue.sit: Once this whole business with the Wild Hunt is over...
Let's go out for a walk...

dialogue.t: Yeah! The Frostmoon Scions have changed since you last saw them. Who knows, you might actually like 'em.
I will consider it...
She seems kinda tired...

dialogue.sit: Probably hasn't spoken this much in a while...

dialogue.t: Either way, thanks for agreeing to help us.
...It wasn't much.
The flowers here... They like guests like you.

quests.description: After repairing the giant cannon and successfully dispersing the Wild Hunt, you make for Hiisi Island to attempt to get some clarity regarding the memories of your spaceship.

quests.title: One There Was, Who Hunted the Moon

dialogue.sit: You relate the gist of your conversation with The Damselette to Lauma (without the Moon Goddess joke.)

dialogue.t: The Rächer of Solnari... I've never heard that name before.
Let's keep this news confidential for the time being. It would only cause even more panic amongst the people of Nod-Krai.
But if this Rerir is as you describe, he will be a truly formidable opponent if we try to take him on by our strength alone...
Yeah... Things might be okay if everyone was willing to work together, but right now...

dialogue.sit: If we don't stick together, we'll be picked off one by one.

dialogue.t: Exactly! Whatever the case, let's start by telling those we can get to join up about the crisis!
As it happens, we have our own reasons to protect Nod-Krai... But even if we didn't, we'd never leave people in the lurch. That ain't our style!
Thank you. The Frostmoon Scions will stand with you to prevent this crisis as best we can.
In addition... I believe that the relationships between the various factions in this land are not cast in stone.
The winds of change are blowing, and we Scions have nowhere to run. Our faith, our sect... all of it is here.
Whether our foe is the Fatui or this Rächer, we must stand our ground and remain true to ourselves, even to the last.

dialogue.sit: Thank you.

dialogue.t: Let's see... Speaking of allies, the Krumkake Craftshop is the closest by, right? Ineffa's sure to help us!
Best let her rest.
For now, please keep the current situation confidential.
Friendly approach detected. We meet again.
Listen, listen, we've got updates on the Wild Hunt situation!
Mmhmm, mmhmm...
Threat level... exceeds expectations.
Pfftooey! Doesn't matter if he's the Rächer of Solnari, or Solari, or whatever. One volley from my cannon and he'll be blown to smithereens!
You were there when we fired it, right? If that isn't the kind of firepower that helps you sleep at night, I don't know what is!
True, but the cannon only works against shambling monsters, right? What if Rerir's super fast?
Well... We'll just get Ineffa to go grab him and tie him down.
You're not taking this seriously at all, are you!?
Anyways... Firepower's not a concern. See those canisters over there? That's all concentrated kuuvahki, which we'll be shipping to Nasha Town.
More than enough ammo in there to blast that Fatui research facility to bits in a single shot!
You... sure have been looking forward to this battle, huh?
Of course! This is gonna be the shot that shocks the world! All Nod-Krai — heck, all of Snezhnaya — will know my name once we're through!

dialogue.sit: In that case, our firepower needs are in your hands.
We'll continue to monitor the Wild Hunt's movements.

dialogue.t: Sure. Travel safe!
Aino, there remains intel left unshared.
Ohhh, right, yeah... Since you're investigating the Wild Hunt, something pretty weird's happened in Nasha Town. Should probably watch out for that once you're back.
Remember that Sousi guy, the Ratnik in charge of firing the cannon? He's... been found dead in their organization's offices.
Wait, what!? Didn't we just see him like... half a day ago?
Yeah. It's still new news, so not many people are in the know. We were only informed because we'd worked together closely... and even then, only just now.
I'll send Ineffa over to Nasha Town with some flowers later... *sigh*
He seemed like a good guy. Didn't put on any airs despite being a superior officer, either.
The data concurs. This gentleman appears to have been one of the most accomplished amongst the Lightkeepers' Sergeant Majors.
His character has also received commendation. Most would have lacked the motivation to fatally attack him.
That makes it even worse...

dialogue.sit: Could it have been the Wild Hunt?
Is Rerir actually afraid of the cannon?

dialogue.t: Hey! What do you mean "actually"?
Either way, I'm not clued in on the details. Only Ratniki have been allowed on-site to investigate the scene. You'll have to find some way in if you want to check it out for yourselves.
Got it. Let's go, then. You coming along, Ineffa?
My tasks are incomplete. The last few batches of ammunition must be randomly inspected. You go ahead.
Alright, we'll see you later!
The wind blows stronger. May your path ahead be smooth.
This must be it. Doesn't look like there's any chance of us getting in with that Ratnik guarding the door, though...
Should we go speak to the guard first?
Might as well try squeezing blood from a stone.
Eh!? Nefer! When did you...
I came over to take a look as soon as I received the news just now. Aino told you about this, then?

dialogue.sit: Yes, while we were passing by the Krumkake Craftshop.

dialogue.t: Before we start, shall we see if we've made the same guess?

dialogue.sit: Looks like the Wild Hunt is on the move.

dialogue.t: Indeed. Quicker than we thought, as well.
Keep your eyes peeled for any clues once we get in. No need to jump to conclusions.
Uh, but how are we supposed to get in at all?
Just follow me.
I'm sorry, but we're not open to guests right now.
Sorry about that. They're here to investigate.
...All of them?
The paperwork checks out.
Alright then, enter.
Batch inspection complete. Approved. Next up...
Hang on. Weren't you supposed to bring me some candy? You said you would!
Err, sorry, but things happened kinda suddenly, so—

dialogue.sit: On the way upstairs to the crime scene, you briefly relate the information about the Rächer of Solnari to Nefer...

dialogue.t: Whew... Paimon might've said this before, Nefer, but you sure do come prepared.
Sieciech, my old friend — fill us in, if you would.
Greetings. If you would allow me...
The murder happened not long ago. The Sergeant Major was killed by a single piercing strike from a polearm. We have performed a preliminary sweep of the crime scene to facilitate investigation.
No obvious signs of a violent struggle, no damaged doors or windows. The culprit must have used some other means to enter the room unopposed before performing the deed.
Entering unopposed... So, do you think there's a chance that the culprit would usually have right of entry?

dialogue.sit: (It could have been Rerir in disguise, like how he turned into Lumine(Aether)...)

dialogue.t: At the moment, the most valuable lead we have is based on an eyewitness report from a nearby resident.
Specifically, that Flins was seen entering and leaving this place in the time period when the crime most likely occurred.
Fl—Flins!?
We have tried to contact him, but he has not replied.
Very odd indeed.
So... He's the prime suspect right now, right?
To be honest, I'm not particularly inclined to believe that this was an inside job. Flins can come across a bit eccentric, but he does well in missions on the whole.
He also had no disagreements with the Sergeant Major that we know of, so he lacks a motive to commit such a terrible crime.
But neither the eyewitness report nor the nature of the fatal wound itself are in his favor... So we are looking for him at present.
Looks like there's not much else to dig up here. Let's go outside and discuss what we've seen.

dialogue.sit: Agreed.

dialogue.t: So, the evidence points to Flins, and he just so happens to have disappeared without a trace. A sticky situation indeed...
We know that this "Flins" could have been Rerir in disguise, but we lack the evidence to prove this to anyone else.
Furthermore, Flins has left us with many questions, all of which will require a reasonable explanation.
Yeah. He said he would report back to headquarters, but it seems he hasn't gone at all. What could he be doing...

dialogue.sit: (The first time I met Flins, I did notice that there was something odd about his lantern... Some power concealed within it.)
(Now that I think about it, that power was somewhat similar to Abyssal energies I've encountered before...)
(In the worst case scenario, "Flins" might be an entirely fabricated entity...)

dialogue.t: Let's approach the issue this way. First, we must determine our culprit. Was it Flins? Or Rerir in disguise?

dialogue.sit: It's got to be the latter...

dialogue.t: Yeah. What reason would Flins have to murder Sousi anyway?
None, as far as I know. And even if he had a motive, it would have been easier to do so out in the wild, rather than in Nasha Town.
Yeah, they would have often gone out on missions together — plenty of chances there.

dialogue.sit: Even if it were Rerir, though...
His motives would be just as unclear.

dialogue.t: Yes, but there's one thing worth noting here. Remember the intel we got back at the tavern? No one has ever seen a phantom that can take the form of other humans within the Wild Hunt.
This means that he has been hesitant to abuse this ability, or allow it to become common knowledge... Likely so that he could act in secret under other guises.
But no matter what, borrowing identities comes with risks, right? What if you bump into the person you're imitating along the way?
Precisely. In other words, his goal must have been worth the risk — similar to how he came in disguise to obtain the Moon Marrow.
He likely knew, then, that the real Flins would not appear and get in his way during this time.

dialogue.sit: And why was he able to determine that?

dialogue.t: We'd have to ask Flins ourselves, I'm afraid. But we shouldn't jump to any conclusions here. We can't discount the possibility that he might actually be the murderer himself — not yet, at least.
And there are other, less likely scenarios — for instance, Rerir may have already killed Flins long ago, and been living as him for some time now...

dialogue.sit: Regardless...
We have to find him.

dialogue.t: Yes. That is our ticket to a breakthrough.
Then we've got to find him before the Lightkeepers do, or we might never see him again...!
Steady now. Our friend should be back soon.
We've tracked him down — to a beach north of Nasha Town. The Wild Hunt is present too, so we're putting a force together.
...I'll have you know that this is top-secret information I'm leaking here.
Don't worry. You'll receive a top-class reward in return.
The beach is all yours. I'll stay and slow the Lightkeepers down — things might go south if you bump into one another.
Oh right, before we go! Should we reveal Rerir's secret?
Since he's trying to keep it all hush-hush, why don't we just pull the curtains on his little trick? That'll teach him to sneak around pretending to be other people!
Hehe...
Hey! Why are you laughing?
Oh, I was just imagining how satisfying that would feel... But I'm afraid this revelation would only stir up more chaos.
Setting aside the matter of evidence, some may trust Flins on our account, whereas others would suspect him on account of his behavior.
Tossing him into a swirling tumult of public opinion like that might just give Rerir more opportunities to capitalize on.
And think about it — once people learn that he can masquerade as those they trust, would they continue to welcome friends into their homes with such open hearts?
Unease grips the hearts of those in Nasha Town already. We should avoid throwing more fuel onto the fire.
...Yeah, you're right. You've really thought of everything, huh? Nothing for it, then. We've just gotta find Flins!
Indeed. But just in case, let me stress once more — we should neither be excessively afraid of "Rerir," nor trust in "Flins" too lightly.
This light source is of special Lightkeeper design. It provides illumination within Wild Hunt anomalies, and can briefly dispel the Abyssal fog within.
Oh, right, we'll have to deal with that mess too... Yeah, this'll be important. Thanks a bunch, Nefer!
You're welcome. I've charged it to your account, by the way.
Hey, you—
This monster was lurking near the lamp... that must've been a planned ambush. We're not falling for that again!
Hmm? There's something inside it, some small device...
Eh? Why isn't it giving off light anymore? Is it broken? We'd better take it with us.
So you were tangling with Rerir out here, all by yourself.
So... That vile phantom hiding inside the Wild Hunt has a name of his own— Argh...

dialogue.sit: Let's find a spot to rest first.

dialogue.t: Yeah, you don't look so good...
...Sorry you had to see me like this. All the same, you have my sincere thanks for your aid.
To think you had the power to so easily cleanse the filth staining the lantern, which tormented me so...
Might I ask what magic that was, or whose pupil you are? I believe I might have saved some face had I mastered just a fraction of such abilities.

dialogue.sit: I don't understand it either. Just my constitution, I think.

dialogue.t: And an enviable constitution it is. A pity that such abilities cannot be acquired.
Why did Abyssal power just burst out of your lantern, anyway...?
That is a long story. Many moons ago, when on Wild Hunt clearance duty, I shattered one of its cores, only for a special crystalline object to fall out.
I sensed a power surging within it that was at once familiar yet strangely illusory...
I freely confess to being an avid collector of ancient gems, coins, and other curios. And curiosity it was that had me store this crystal inside my lantern.
Afterwards, I wound up collecting a few more such crystals quite by accident, and discovered that they could merge into a single piece without my prompting... Though my understanding ends there.
It was only recently that they began slowly emitting Abyssal energy, which could neither be dispelled nor weakened.
Is that what Rerir claimed belonged to him? That must be what he's after, then.
I concur. And here's the kicker... Before, he was exceedingly weak. In fact, I've already beaten him several times, though I could not destroy him completely.
But I noticed while engaging him that the crystal fragment would restrict my powers. As such, it occurred to me that I should hide it rather than tangle with him any longer.
Alas, he has proved most fixated upon this fragment, and for some reason, his strength has grown by leaps and bounds since I last encountered him.

dialogue.sit: If this object is contaminated by the Abyss...
...Why carry it on your person?

dialogue.t: And where, might I ask, would it be safe? Or do you think it wiser I threw it away?
Were our places switched, would you discard it, knowing that its perilous might was beyond your ability to counteract, yet capable of causing greater harm should it lie beyond your grasp?

dialogue.sit: Probably not.

dialogue.t: Yeah! Throwing it away would mean giving the bad guy what he wants! But exposing yourself to its corrosion and growing weaker by the day... That sounds super dangerous, too...
Only those who shoulder risks are qualified to welcome in the turning of the tide. Those who flee when troubles come are nothing more than deserters...
Though I shan't deny that I have your fortuitous arrival, and most outstanding assistance, to thank for my continued ability to speak such platitudes.
Either way, it seems this fragment is now utterly still. That must have made it useless to Rerir — I doubt he would have retreated so readily otherwise.
I imagine this wasn't the only reason you came looking for me, though...?
Uh, well, no, but...

dialogue.sit: You briefly tell Flins about Rerir's murder of Sousi, and about the subsequent attempt to frame him.

dialogue.t: Ah... I see.

dialogue.sit: Can you think of a reason why Rerir would try to frame you?

dialogue.t: To use the Lightkeepers to find me, I suspect. I did not inform anyone of my true whereabouts, so he should have had more difficulty tracking me down.
They alone have the ability to quickly pinpoint my position. Our Sergeant Major has a kuuvahki-powered device that can be used to detect others who bear a lantern.
They usually don't pay my whereabouts much mind, unless they absolutely must find me.
Uh, you mean this thing?
Yes. Where did you pick this up?
We found it inside a lantern when we first charged into the Wild Hunt anomaly.
It must belong to a Ratnik dispatched to investigate the area... who, it seems, dropped everything and fled the moment they saw the Wild Hunt massing to strike. Well, at least they're not dead.
Guess it's not surprising how they found you so fast, then. But... If Rerir could've shapeshifted into Sousi, why didn't he just use that kuuvahki device to find you himself?
Were he to use it, that device would likely fail to act as it should — owing to Abyssal interference.
Ahhh, guess that explains it...
So... Not only is this Rerir ruthless, but a purveyor of dirty tricks too.
You might not be familiar with Sergeant Major Sousi, but he put his heart and soul into every mission.
Our deployments are subject to orders from headquarters, and his orders were to be stationed long-term in Nasha Town. As such, he was very seldom able to go back and visit his family.
He worked so, so hard, seeking to produce excellent results that might convince them to transfer him out.
Oh...
But every year, they would say, "Wait a little longer." "Wait a little longer." He often wondered if it was because he was lacking somehow.
In truth, everyone had nothing but the highest praise for him. But good work does not always lead to good outcomes.
The higher-ups would think, "He's doing great where he is. Let him stay there forever." A most convenient choice, for them at least.
Whereas his subordinates would think, "Wouldn't it be a shame if we were to lose such a talented, easygoing boss?"
So he waited, and he waited. Until the world closed its eyes in the depths of the night, and a lantern was slowly lit for him alone, that no one could see.

dialogue.sit: It's a tragic story.

dialogue.t: One that has played out many times throughout history.
...Another reason to take this Rerir's head.
*sigh* At least we now know that he's looking for these fragments inside Wild Hunt anomalies...
And yet, what did the Sergeant Major have to do with any of this? Why did he have to die?
Could Rerir be angry that the cannon Sousi set up to fire destroyed the fragments he wanted to collect?
Hmm... Could you take me to the scene of the crime?

dialogue.sit: Probably...
...But you are a suspect in this case.

dialogue.t: We shall just have to exercise some discretion, then. Come on, let us be on our way.
I understand the situation, more or less. Much has happened, I see.
Either way, I suppose we were lucky not to receive a "warm welcome" on the way over here. It seems my fellow Lightkeepers do not wish to make this case public just yet.
Yeah... Guess Nasha Town's already been enough of a mess lately.
Let's stop here. Any further, and the Ratniki might detect us.
Since you two can enter, I'll have to request that you kindly "pick me up" once you're inside...
Oh? And how are we supposed to do that...?
You'll know when the time comes. See you later.
Ugh, still acting all mysterious... But he seemed pretty confident, so guess we gotta trust him.
H—Hello...
Ah, you're the special assistants for this investigation, right?
Yup, that's us.

dialogue.sit: Sorry, I know it's a bit late...
But there's a couple of things we'd like to take a look at.

dialogue.t: Well, you're just in time. We're basically done investigating the crime scene. All that's left is to finish writing up some records, then properly dispose of Sergeant Major Sousi's remains.
If there's anything else you'd like to look into, this is your last chance to do so.

dialogue.sit: Find anything new?

dialogue.t: Sadly, no. The motive behind the killing remains a mystery, and while we somehow managed to get news of Flins, an unexpected accident caused us to miss him.
But considering that Nefer from the Curatorium of Secrets came forward to help investigate, I have no doubt that a breakthrough's not far off.

dialogue.sit: (Expert use of delaying tactics on her part. Excellent work...)

dialogue.t: We'll do our part too! Alright, we're going in. Seeya later!
Phew, we're in — thanks to Nefer's reputation, once again.
But we still know nothing about how Flins is gonna enter, or how we'll pick him up... never mind how we'll leave later on.
Is something the matter, {NICKNAME}?

dialogue.sit: There's a strange light by the window.

dialogue.t: Huh, that looks like Flins's lantern... But where is he, exactly?
Well, we've got the lantern. What now?
Waa— Ergh, Paimon almost screamed out loud! You never said you could do magic like that!

dialogue.sit: Now that's what I call going incognito.

dialogue.t: This lantern may have a rather peculiar shape, but so long as it doesn't glow, it won't stand out in the dark.
I calculated that you would have already entered, so I chose a spot visible from the window before using light to send you a signal.
As I thought, you're both sharp-eyed and on the ball.
Hehe, the perks of being veteran adventurers, huh?

dialogue.sit: What you just did... Surely that can't be accomplished through elemental power alone?

dialogue.t: Your composure is more impressive still. You're right. That required a little... trick of my own.
But let us leave such trivial topics for a more relaxed moment. Our time is limited, after all.
Hmm. Just as I thought... Come, try sensing it yourself.

dialogue.sit: (It's very faint, but there is some residual power near the wound that feels identical to the Abyssal energy that surged from Flins's lantern.)

dialogue.t: Identical powers must flow from the same source. It was the Wild Hunt, then, that took my form and killed the Sergeant Major... but why do this?
To sow chaos by depriving the Lightkeepers of one of their commanders?

If the Wild Hunt's true form is powerful enough to stand against the world as you claim, I fear not even the full force of Lightkeepers could stand against him, let alone the handful of us stationed in Nasha Town.
He would have no reason whatsoever to pick quarrels with individual "ants."
Let's look again more closely. We must leave no stone unturned.

dialogue.sit: They said that the crime scene investigation is already complete.
There should no longer be a need to keep this place exactly as-is.

dialogue.t: Well, that makes things simpler. In that case, allow me to disturb the fallen. May the ghost-flame guide your spirit, may you rest in peace...

dialogue.sit: However, despite a very thorough search, few new clues emerge.

dialogue.t: When we fought, he seemed like quite a reckless foe — certainly not the meticulous mastermind type. Yet here we are, grappling with this enigma he has left us...
If we can't get any leads, we might have to go back and find Nefer...
Ugh, the longer we're stuck here, the likelier he is to achieve his goal... This is so frustrating.

dialogue.sit: (Is that all? Have we really tried every angle, found every clue?)
Paimon, look at the flashing light on his arm.

dialogue.t: You mean this...?
I'm not well-versed in machinery... but that means his mechanical arm is malfunctioning, right? It might have been broken in combat...
No, that's not right. Paimon remembers this signal. We saw it before while repairing the cannon.
It doesn't mean that the components are damaged. It just means that they're due for regular maintenance, so the device has stopped operating...
But the real problem is that—

dialogue.sit: When we were fixing the cannon...
...His arm was working just fine.

dialogue.t: Yeah... He even helped us find the maintenance port!
It could still be a coincidence, but considering it hasn't been long at all since we were repairing that cannon...
...The Sousi you met could have been Rerir in disguise. In other words, he played the Sergeant Major before disguising himself as me.
That's right! If only there was some way to prove it...

dialogue.sit: If something needed maintenance...
You'd go register it with Nasha Town's repairman.

dialogue.t: You mean Hintsa?
We had a short chat with him once at the tavern, but it's so late... Guess it'll have to wait till tomorrow.
I know where he lives. The situation is critical, so let us now take up the role of uninvited guests ourselves.
Ah, yes, and one more thing...
Remember to "pick me up" by the window.
*yawn* ...Ah, it's you two... and Flins. Given the hour, I guess it must be an emergency?
It is indeed. Our sincerest apologies for interrupting your rest.
We're investigating a certain matter in connection with Sergeant Major Sousi. We'd like to know if he has sent you a request for maintenance to be performed on his mechanical arm.
