Sousi... Oh. So the rumors I heard... are they true?
*sigh*... You know what? Forget it... I'm sure it's complicated. No further questions from me. Just a moment — I need to check my records.
Thank you for your understanding.
Got it. Eight days ago, he came to request a round of regular maintenance, but as it happened, I had run out of the required components.
His mechanical arm is especially sophisticated, having been designed by Aino personally. The parts, too, could only be made by her.
As such, they usually take several days to arrive. In fact, this time, he even asked me if we could push his request forward.

And I understood, completely. Not being able to use your hand... That's rough for anyone, but even more so if your job involves fighting out in the wild. So I did my best to convince Aino to rush the job...
And eventually, the parts arrived — three days ago, if I remember correctly. I sent word to the Lightkeepers immediately, but he never showed up. I assumed he was just out on some mission or other...
Uh... What's with those faces? Everything alright?
You've provided us with some very crucial information, Hintsa. You have our thanks.
We can't make everything public yet, but once our investigation is complete, I will return to thank you and provide an explanation on behalf of all the Lightkeepers.
No worries. Just glad I could help.
Thanks. Good night!
Good night. Hope the investigation goes well.
It seems that it is as we guessed. The "Sergeant Major Sousi" you encountered while repairing the cannon was actually Rerir in disguise.
Eight days ago, he had yet to act, but at some point after that, he attacked and imprisoned the Sergeant Major.
With the immense gap in strength between them, the job was finished in a single blow — and thus, Rerir had no opportunity to discover the malfunctioning mechanical arm.

Perhaps his mastery of shapeshifting extends only to outward form — and not, therefore, to complex internal mechanisms. Hence his oversight of the uniquely mechanical traits of the Sergeant Major's arm, and in turn, this flaw in his disguise.
You're saying he thought no one would realize his mechanical arm was actually made of some kinda black muck on the inside, so long as it worked, right?
Hmm. Still seems like there's a lot of guesswork involved here, but it mostly makes sense...

dialogue.sit: That means that the only thing he did as Sousi...
...Was fire the cannon.

dialogue.t: This also has me stumped for the moment. The cannon has always been used to destroy the Wild Hunt, and it works as intended.
But how would that help Rerir, exactly...?
Assuming he plans to collect the fragments within Wild Hunt anomalies, firing the cannon works against him, since it would blast those fragments to smithereens.
Ugh, so we solved one mystery only to dig up another...
This is getting Paimon kinda down... *yawn* and sleepy, too...

dialogue.sit: We've been on edge for too long, it seems.

dialogue.t: Yes, I'd say it is high time we took a break. Seems like there's a lot left to investigate.
We'll have to fight Rerir eventually — and we'll do a poor job if we're not well-rested.
Yeah, we should totally get some sleep first...

dialogue.sit: Want to rest a day in Nasha Town?
Your residence is quite far away.

dialogue.t: A reasonable suggestion. I have no doubt that my quarters have been turned inside out by now, at any rate.
My colleagues have never failed to live up to my expectations of their discourtesy.
W—Well, guess we'll just have to "pick you up" as usual...
That would be good, yes. Feel free to put the room costs on my tab.
Whew, back inside! We can finally take a breather! Okay, Paimon, in and out!
Haha, I suppose we could all take a moment to unwind. Hmm, as I recall, our first meeting took place not far from here. Ah, the nostalgia.
Had you already sensed the unique power within my lantern at that time?

dialogue.sit: Yes, which is why I asked you to give it to me.

dialogue.t: I see. Ah, words truly do fail to capture your superlative insight.
Fortunate, then, that Abyssal energy was only leaking from the fragment in miniscule amounts when we first met, or I might have been in for a real interrogation.
Yeah... Hard to say how that would've played out. We've had a whole bunch of unpleasant run-ins with the Abyss...

dialogue.sit: Rerir seems fixated on you...
...And you, on him.

dialogue.t: You mean to ask why I'm going this far to oppose him? Well, as a Lightkeeper, I'd say I'm simply doing my job.

dialogue.sit: Come on, don't play games with me.

dialogue.t: Yeah! You're covered in more mysteries than Paimon could shake a skewer at. You can't just get out of explaining yourself by making lame excuses!
Hmm, alright. I suppose I do owe you some honesty, whether out of gratitude or the need to build trust.
Your deductions have been quite correct. Should one wish to conceal oneself within a lantern, elemental power alone is not enough.
You know humans well, and naturally, you understand their limits.
But some things that humans would consider difficult are quite normal in the eyes of non-humans.
So you mean you're one of the latter?
Have you heard of how Snezhnaya was once the realm of the fae?
This race is no longer of any importance, but they still exist — as evidenced by the fact that I am standing before you.
We've heard some scattered legends, but... that's all Paimon thought there was to it.
I once turned my heart toward humanity, and thus did I experience loss. I once labored and did much, and put an end to my tale with my own hands.
When you realize you are floating in the middle of a vast ocean, you cannot help but feel that swimming in any direction would be equally meaningless.
Would it not be better, then, to simply sink?
But before I could sink to truly lightless depths, chance had it that I should be awakened by a band of Ratniki.
They were facing a horde of Abyssal monsters, and could not last against such a disparity in strength, yet none fled.
Those who dwell in darkness for long enough become exceedingly sensitive to all light — and the first light I saw upon awakening was that which shone from their eyes.
Is that why you chose to help them?
Perhaps I was moved by their valor. Perhaps I simply saw my past self in them, and was moved to action for the first time in a long, long while.
But I was freshly awoken, and my powers were limited. I could not prevent casualties altogether.
The survivors and I buried the fallen heroes... That was the origin of the "Final Night Cemetery."

dialogue.sit: And that's why you chose to become a Lightkeeper...

dialogue.t: Well, not exactly. I was just more familiar with them, so joining up seemed the most convenient way to experience human life.
Doesn't sound too believable...
Well, I believe it. Besides, I'm well past the age when one might believe in "things that must be done."
Nonetheless, there are still some things I will not allow to happen. The chaos that Rerir has been stirring up is one of them.
Tomorrow, I shall go and check our records to see if I can find any connection between the Wild Hunt, Rerir, and the cannon.
Will you need us to get you where you need to be?
Oh, I'll be fine. I keep a backup copy at my residence in case of emergencies.
Can... you even go back there right now? Won't there be Ratniki watching it?

Thanks for the reminder. I believe they'll have checked my place, but they won't have stayed. All things are ranked according to their priority, and we lack the manpower for such an open-ended stakeout.
And even if someone is waiting, I have ways around that. I am the master of my own house, after all.
Alright then, we'll trust you. *yawn* We sure ended up chatting for a while, huh? Paimon's super tired now, but... Y'know, feels like we can breathe easier, now that we know you better.
Haha. I didn't take you for the cautious sort.
Anyway, I hope you'll help me keep this a secret. I'd prefer others not to know about my past unless strictly necessary, nor do I want to attract more trouble on account of being a fae.

dialogue.sit: Don't worry, I won't say a thing.

dialogue.t: Paimon's lips are sealed too!
Alright. Thanks again for your help. Good night, you two.

quests.description: With The Damselette, you not only uncover surprising truths from your memories but also learn the true identity of the phantom masquerading as your sibling. He may well be one of the Five Sinners Dainsleif once mentioned — Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari.

quests.title: The Ashen-White Order Burns

dialogue.t: Ergh, so much noise... What's going on this time...
Hey! Where's Flins!? Is he here, or isn't he?
We would be most obliged if you would pipe down a little, dear guest. Our other guests are resting...
Resting!? We're all about to be done for, and you're talking about rest!?
Flins is a Wild Hunt shapeshifter, here to deceive us all! If we don't get rid of him now, there'll be no end to this!
You'd better give him up — if anything happens, your business here is done for. You want that, huh?
Or are you in cahoots with him? You with the Wild Hunt too, huh?
What happened? Did something leak out?
But we were so careful last night... How did anyone see us?

dialogue.sit: Something fishy about this...
I doubt it's because of anything we did.

dialogue.t: Wh—What do you mean?

dialogue.sit: They clearly know something...
Why else would they be talking about a "Wild Hunt shapeshifter"?

dialogue.t: This is so confusing... What do we do? These people are no match for Flins, but they're super heated right now...
It's not like all the unusual stuff about him will make it any easier to explain, either.

dialogue.sit: Let's go buy some time.

dialogue.t: Okay!
Hey! Let us in, now!
My apologies, my apologies.
Hold on! Calm down, everyone!
What in Teyvat is the meaning of this racket? Are you intent on depriving both the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets of even a moment's rest?
Boss, do we really have to entertain people who don't respect the rules? Call a few of your boys and have them thrown out.
And what hole did you crawl out of?

A watering hole, of course — the one you've just disturbed. A place to get a moment's respite from all the recent unhappiness, and to escape from all this talk of the Wild Hunt, or strange ghosts and phantoms.
Who'd have guessed people like you would come bursting in, shrieking louder than any ghoul?
Tch. This is a matter of utmost importance! We've got solid evidence. All we need now is to confront Flins, face-to-face!
Exactly! And you sure don't look like an impartial party either, Nefer.
Oh, don't I now? How about this then, Boss? Let them do their search. If they find their man, they can have their little chat.
But if they don't, then they owe everyone here an apology — as well as compensation for all the racket they've caused.
Wait, it's... Huh?
Alright, alright... I suppose that's the only way. If we don't let them in now, they'll be back sooner or later... *sigh* What a mess.
Oh, alright then...
Well? I'd say that sounds like an impartial proposal. What say you? Or are you suddenly unsure of yourselves?
Hmph. Come on, everyone. Move it!
...No sign of Flins...
B—But... How can that be? Hasn't he always stayed here!?
Done searching, are we? Guess it's time to uphold your end of the bargain, huh?
Waaaaaah!

dialogue.sit: After teaching the group a harsh lesson, Nefer finally lets them go. You leave the area as well.

dialogue.t: So, Paimon. You've been waiting to ask me something, haven't you?
Yeah, uhh... How did they even find us here?
My inside man with the Lightkeepers informed me that you paid the crime scene a late-night visit. I surmised that you must have rendezvoused with Flins and obtained some new information.
Then, early this morning, a group of people gathered at the town gates, news spreading amongst them that the Wild Hunt could disguise itself by taking on familiar faces.
Everyone started throwing out the names of possible suspects — no one, seemingly, was exempt.
And amidst it all, Flins's name started gaining more and more traction. I'm sure his solitary lifestyle may have played a part, but I wouldn't discount Rerir throwing fuel on the fire in secret.
So, did Flins make his escape after hearing about this?
Hehe. And that's where I — Jahoda, the quick-witted, fleet-footed backbone of the Curatorium — got my chance to shine!
While everyone was super focused on the argument in the main hall, I alone noticed an opening—
I got her to climb up to a window to help Flins out, only for her to return with nothing but a lantern.
...Aw, come on, Boss, I was just getting started!
We initially intended to bring Flins back to the Curatorium and wait those people out, but I never expected this to be all that was left.
I imagine, though, that he wouldn't have left something that was so seemingly important to him behind.
Might he intend to come back and get it later? Maybe... I'm not sure.
W—Well, he's outta harm's way now, so that's not super important, right?
Oh?
What Paimon means to say is... We've got lots of new intel to share!
Hmm... Alright then. Jahoda, contact the others. We're going to need all hands on deck.
Let's have this discussion over at my place.
It's getting late. The situation is urgent, but rest is vital. Good night, both of you.
(test)准备好了吗？
I see. So Flins has a fragment taken from within a Wild Hunt anomaly...
Is he gonna be okay now that he's on his own again?
Earlier, he said that the fragment had gone still, so it's probably of no use to Rerir now.
In that case, Rerir shouldn't have any reason to keep pursuing him, right? So was all that ruckus back at The Flagship just an act of spite, or what?
If I were him, I would have simply turned my attention to collecting other fragments.
A reasonable course of action. Remember what we heard back at the tavern, {NICKNAME}? The actual number of Wild Hunt anomalies destroyed has been greater than Lightkeeper records would indicate.
Some of these must have been Rerir's doing. He must have been seeking more fragments.
This much is pretty easy to understand... But why would he pretend to be Sousi and put so much effort into getting the cannon up and running again?
Maybe 'cause that'd be more efficient than having to clear anomalies himself?

dialogue.sit: Flins mentioned that if the cannon were fired at the Wild Hunt...
...The fragments would be blasted into oblivion too.

dialogue.t: Yeah, I'm confident that the ammo we're packing has the oomph to do that. But I am a mechanic, after all — for me, test data and their conclusions speak loudest.
Why don't we find a few of those fragments ourselves and use kuuvahki to carry out a little experiment?
Our lab could certainly accommodate such a test.
In other words, we gotta destroy a couple of anomalies and collect fragments from them, right?
Lightkeeper operations have just about ceased following the Sergeant Major's passing.
Meanwhile, the Wild Hunt continues to grow in scale by the day... I fear only we can keep the situation under control now.
Then we'd best act fast. Paimon's got a bad feeling about this...
A feeling we all share, I'm afraid.

dialogue.sit: (The fragments, the cannon, kuuvahki, Rerir, and the Abyss... There must be some thread linking all these factors together.)
(Besides, is getting revenge on Flins truly Rerir's sole aim?)
(We're missing some decisive connection here, but we're running out of time.)

dialogue.t: There are three Wild Hunt sites that must be dealt with urgently... But I believe we have the capacity to handle it.

dialogue.sit: Since that's the case...
I'd like to investigate something on the Lightkeepers' end one more time.

dialogue.t: Works for me. Ineffa and I will take our workshop assistants to deal with one of the sites.
The Curatorium will handle another.
And we Frostmoon Scions shall deal with the remaining one.
Heh, Paimon didn't think she'd ever get to see everyone here carrying out a plan together like this...
Never mind you — this is a first for me, too...
Let's head out, then. We'll meet back up at my lab with the fragments.

dialogue.sit: If you run into Rerir, do not engage him.
He's grown much stronger since our last encounter.

dialogue.t: Understood.
Time is of the essence now. Our foe could make his next move at any moment, so we must stay in contact with one another.
Gotcha. Stay safe, everyone!
Huh...
Anyone seen the lantern? Has Flins dropped by already?
No one's guarding this place, just like he said. But, uh, where do we find the information he mentioned?
This way.
Let's move. We're running out of time.
Ah, there you are! Okay, let's split up and make this happen...
...Or not! How are we supposed to read through this many files!?

dialogue.sit: Yeah, this might be...

dialogue.t: Difficult, yes, but it is also our most efficient option.
To expose the true intentions of this Rerir, we need to dive into Nod-Krai's history.
*sigh* Hope we don't land on our heads, then...
Ahh! Gh—Ghost!

dialogue.sit: What's the matter?

dialogue.t: That file s—s—suddenly moved by itself!
This is a graveyard, right, Flins? D—Do these things just kinda... happen?
Many strange things happen here, but this is not one of them.
B—But that file really did m—m—move by itself!
Hey, come out! D—Don't scare Paimon like that!

dialogue.sit: (I don't sense anything.)

dialogue.t: Hmm? "Wild Hunt Phenomena Log"? Hmm...
Hey, another file's moving!

dialogue.sit: With a similar title, too...

dialogue.t: Are we... being given hints? I feel no hostility. On the contrary — it seems we're being aided, somehow.
Really? H—Hey, seriously, another one? O—Okay, then... Paimon'll read this one!
Phew, finally finished! Paimon sure could use a long break from long words now... Hope she can remember it all.
The material I've read through has all been about past Wild Hunt incidents of enormous scale. What about you?

dialogue.sit: Pretty much the same here.

dialogue.t: Paimon as well! Guess that makes three of us.
Hmm. Whatever this is, it seems to want us to notice something. Let's bring our files together and give them another look through.
Alright, Paimon'll go fetch hers!
Hmm, all these incidents look pretty different...
Wait, I've noticed something. Before the occurrence of these huge Wild Hunt events, a smaller-scale one would erupt in the exact same location.
And look — all these smaller-scale Wild Hunt site reports share a common outcome.
They'd be detected, but would go inactive before any forces could be sent to deal with them. They could then be sealed directly using a Tideseal Stone... Eh, but why?

dialogue.sit: Was Rerir actively clearing these sites?

dialogue.t: Some of these records are too old. I doubt he had regained the ability to act freely yet, or we would have met long ago.
Ah, and here's another similarity! "Kuuvahki in nearby soil completely drained." Could this be important, somehow?
Kuuvahki and the Wild Hunt are mutually opposed forces.
We Lightkeepers previously believed that these small Wild Hunt sites would temporarily go inactive due to being neutralized by the kuuvahki present in the soil.
But now that we've synthesized all this data, there is a key issue this hypothesis cannot explain...

dialogue.sit: If the Wild Hunt's power had already been neutralized...
...Why would another large-scale Wild Hunt occur soon after?

dialogue.t: Indeed. Despite the name, I would not call a Tideseal Stone's sealing powers "watertight," exactly — but for it to fail and the situation to deteriorate in such short order...
Urgh... Paimon feels like she's almost got it...

dialogue.sit: (The Wild Hunt was not suppressed by kuuvahki. Instead, it became stronger...)
(And Rerir wants to use Aino's cannon, the ammo of which is also made using kuuvahki...)
(Could it be—!?)
He can use kuuvahki?

dialogue.t: Yes, that might be it. It could be that when kuuvahki and Abyssal energies meet, the stronger side will suppress the weaker one.
And while kuuvahki can indeed destroy small-scale Wild Hunt anomalies, should Rerir be strong enough... the kuuvahki might be his for the taking instead.
P—Paimon kinda gets where we're going with this!

dialogue.sit: The Abyss always seeks to corrupt...
This is just like the Abyssal threat the ancient dragons faced.

dialogue.t: What are you referring to?
We had a real close encounter with the Abyss in Natlan. It's a force that tries to taint everything... Ergh, it's hard to explain in detail, but basically, your reasoning makes sense!

dialogue.sit: So Rerir also grew stronger...
...On account of the cannon being fired?

dialogue.t: Was there a gap between him pretending to be Sergeant Major Sousi and the cannon being fired?
There was! Aino needed to make some adjustments after we finished those repairs. Rerir, disguised as Sousi, left at that point...

...Leaving him more than enough time to shapeshift into you, return to the Lightkeepers' office, and set up the crime scene, before heading over to the cannon's target area and absorbing the kuuvahki.
It all makes sense... And all that, just for the fragment I had with me.
It begs the question: What makes it so special that he needs it so badly?

dialogue.sit: That's... still a mystery.

dialogue.t: *knocking*
Hmm? That's odd. We shouldn't have any guests.
I'll go take a look.
Ah, it's... an ibis.
It's carrying a letter! Ooh, Lauma must've sent it. She can speak to little animals.
Let's see here...
"Situation Urgent: The cannon began operating shortly after we left Nasha Town, and is preparing to fire."
"It is locked on to Starsand Shoal. Please return to Nasha Town and assist with all haste. Lauma."
That's gotta be Rerir's doing! But why's he using the cannon again? Didn't he already fire it once before?
No time for speculation. He's already made his preparations. If you recall, his body was incomplete when we last met.
If this bombardment continues to increase his strength, he might regain his "complete" form.

dialogue.sit: A "complete" Sinner...

dialogue.t: Wh—What should we do? There's no way we're getting back to Nasha Town in time!

dialogue.sit: We'll just have to trust them.

dialogue.t: ...Let's go to the cannon's target site. That's where we should find Rerir — and that's where we'll stop him.
One moment, just let me get this news to Lauma. Nasha Town is in their hands now.
Go, fly! Not a moment to lose!
You're here. As expected.
Humans... You never change. Always trying to use powers you neither comprehend nor control.
But it is also thanks to you that I found a way to return.
You've messed with the cannon again, huh? Sorry, but this round's not gonna go your way!
Ah, hahaha... Such faith in your companions.
But will the inhabitants of Nasha Town understand why they wish to stop the cannon? I think not.
When all they see is the Wild Hunt surging up everywhere they look, the cannon must seem like their only lifeline.
This is the truth I have revealed to them.

dialogue.sit: So that's why you riled them all up...
...You were baiting them into firing the cannon.

dialogue.t: They did this all of their own volition.
The zealous worship of power leads only to annihilation of equally zealous proportions. True power does not heed the commands of the weak.
You were waiting for us to leave Nasha Town, then.
Of course. I imagine the one you call "Aino" would have managed to stop the cannon otherwise. Shame, then, that you proved one step too slow.

In their folly, the townspeople will bar the path of all who seek to stop the cannon — and your kind-hearted, weak companions have not the stomach to deal with them. The cannon will not be stopped now.
Well, sir, you look most pleased with yourself. In that case, before you put us out of our misery, I would like to ask you a question, if I may.
See this fragment? It once haunted your dreams, but now, it seems useless to you. What is it, exactly?
Hmph. That... is my corpse.
S—Sorry, what!?
My body was once torn into countless pieces and hurled into the swirling chaos of time itself. But even so, my life and will were not extinguished.
Ah... Every last fragment calls to me. Sooner or later, they shall welcome my return.
What are you even saying...?
Huh, so the terror of the Wild Hunt was, in fact, caused by scattered pieces of your corpse... I guess they don't call you one of the Five Sinners for nothing.
Hmph. Serendipity guided the fragments to construct an incomplete version of myself, upon which I began collecting more within Wild Hunt sites across the land...
But each time, the fragments I obtained were hardly worth mentioning.
While that which you hold in your hand... was my heart.
So that's why it responded so strongly to you.
Only by retrieving this most critical piece could I gain mastery over the turbulent kuuvahki energies and be fully reborn.
Hence you fired that first shot hoping to regain enough power to seize the fragment from me.
Are you completely crazy? Weren't you afraid of dying?

Dying? Hahaha... Such power has no hope of killing me. It may destroy my form over and over, yet always, I rebuild it. It may smash my flesh and crush my bones, thousands of times and more, but that is of no consequence to me.
What truly infuriates me, however, is how you've destroyed my heart. All that suffering, everything I endured... and all for nothing!

dialogue.sit: Wanna go for another round, then?
It's going to turn out the same, you know.

dialogue.t: I have adapted to the strength and flow of this kuuvahki. The next cannon shot will multiply my strength immeasurably.
It will not be a full restoration, no. But it will be more than enough to destroy any in this world who stand in my way.
Still, I suspect the kuuvahki will have rendered you down to nutrients for my consumption well before you have the time to kneel before me.
{NICKNAME}...
Behind you... Look at that light...
Dang it, who fired up the cannon without my say-so!?
Its defensive barrier has also been activated, likely in anticipation of interference by malicious actors.
The air is thick with fear and anxiety... It's spooking the birds and beasts. What exactly is going on?
You're here. Looks like this was all part of Rerir's plan. Not only did he plant seeds of suspicion in people's hearts... Seems he's now igniting them.
Jahoda's gone in to scout out the situation. She'll be back any minute—
I'm back, I'm back! Oh, it's bad out there. Rumors flying everywhere you turn... Something about the Wild Hunt preparing to spawn a wave of monsters, the likes of which we've never seen before...
...But that's not even the worst of it.
Lots of folks don't even believe the cannon can prevent this crisis, so they're getting ready to make a run for it. Others are trying to make a quick buck out of this whole mess...
How could they still be thinking about Mora when such a catastrophe is imminent...?
Unprecedented danger brings unprecedented opportunities in its wake... A chaotic situation can bury much wrongdoing.
Even those who flee without reserve put themselves at the mercy of the divine. Is it any wonder, then, that some will aim to profit?
After all, a gamble that might rewrite one's entire life is hard to come by.
Even so...
Well, seeing as you disapprove of their actions so strongly, Lady Moonchanter, I suggest that you be the one to handle them. Not like that's the only major problem on our plate right now...

Affirmative. We must quell the chaos in Nasha Town as soon as possible. Also, the unexpected activation of the cannon entails a high risk of incorrect operation. This must be stopped in a timely manner.
Well, about that... People have been talking about how someone might come to stop the cannon. They've decided they won't let anyone in.
What!? I made that thing! They can't just take it from me! Let me over there — what are they gonna do, stop me?
They might, if Rerir has already formulated some countermeasure.
For example, he might have spread a rumor that the Wild Hunt would take your form...
Ugh...
Possibility: High. If they view the cannon as Nasha Town's only hope, they are likely to conclude that anyone who tries to stop it must be with the Wild Hunt.
We will face strong resistance, but they are just ordinary people. Brute force must be avoided if possible.
There's no time. Let's go into the town. I'll find some way to calm the townspeople, you find a way to stop the cannon.
Oh, you're back. Mm? And you have a letter?
...{NICKNAME} won't make it back in time, so they're heading straight over to Starsand Shoal instead.
Wait, what? Isn't that the cannon's target? Why would he(she) go there!?
Assessing Risk Level: Maximum.
So if we can't prevent the cannon from being fired...
Then he's(she's) prepared for the worst...
And we must ensure that his(her) trust in us is not misplaced. Let's go.
Most of those we've met so far have been attempting to escape, so they haven't gotten in our way. But it won't be so easy from here on out.
Looks like they've formed groups to protect the cannon. If they believe that we're with the Wild Hunt, we'll have no choice but to force our way through.
Is that... Lady Lauma? But... are you... really her?
Ah, it's you, Ryksa. I believe you recognize this power, having lived on Hiisi Island for so long. It is not something that anyone else could imitate.
I do, yes... So it really is you, my Lady.
But why are you here? Really, I... I believe you, but the others... Well, they'll be on high alert.
The townspeople have been misled into believing that they needed to activate the cannon. I am here to stop them.
But...
I know what you wish to say. Our island and Nasha Town have never had close ties. There should be no reason for me to intervene.
But you chose to leave the island — you had the resolve and the courage to start a new life.
It is unfair — unjust — that you should be dragged into this mess just as that life was about to begin.
I seek to redress this injustice, not only for you, but for everyone here who wishes to live their lives free from this chaos.
Please, have faith in our longstanding friendship... and that this is where my heart has led me.
...Thank you, my Lady, thank you... Please, help us.
Then come. I need you to step forward alongside me, and to do your part too.
Alright. I understand!
Hah, seems we chose the right person for the job. Alright, everyone — let us meet again later.
Huh? You're not coming with us?
We won't be able to calm this storm by our power alone. As such, I'll need to contact some... Let's call them friends in high places, shall we?
Let's go, Jahoda.
O—Okay...! See you again, everyone... Um, that is, if we can...
Lady Moonchanter, there's a child here!
It's alright now. Go, quickly.
Thank you for bringing us here. We can quickly overcome the barrier by going upward from over there.
The cannon is all yours now.
Got it. Thanks, Lauma. Ineffa, give her a krumkake.
Orders received and immediately deferred. Departure takes priority—
Please, everyone, listen to me.
I will not deny that we hold different beliefs, but in the face of the immense threat that hangs above us all, we must persist in trusting one another.
Otherwise, rifts will surely form, prized open by those who harbor ulterior motives.
If your fear is born of helplessness, if you flee because you know not how to fight, then follow me, you who are lost.
I am no god, but so long as we hold our candles steady and unite beneath the same moonlight, no deception or rumors can be concealed from us.
Let us resolve, then, to defend ourselves — and to stand firm against the false illusions by which our foe seeks to beguile us!

This isn't good, Ineffa. We gotta hurry!
Scanning... Kuuvahki ammunition fully loaded. Preheating complete. The cannon is going through its final pre-fire checks.
*sigh* ... Alright. Let's hit the emergency brake.
Assessment: Not enough time. Emergency brake will cause internal explosion of stored kuuvahki. Damage assessment: Incalculable. Nasha Town likely to be blasted skyward.
No, no! I mean a manual brake. You know, the primitive kind.
A "manual brake"... Understood. Roger that.
Hah... Well, that's not good.
Sluggish, torpid... This body is a disappointment.
I can barely muster... Tsk, ten percent of my original strength... You've ruined everything, again...
Let me guess... You didn't get a human body back, did you?
Hah... Urrgh... Raaaarghhh!!
Ahh! What's with him!?

dialogue.sit: (This is bad! His presence feels completely different now... He's even stronger than before!)

dialogue.t: Vedrfolnir...! Rhinedottir...! Arrghh... Tholindis! Tholindis!
Watch out! Whatever rationality he still had when he was searching for his body is gone... All that's left is the calamity you see before you, a monster fueled by nothing but his own obsession!
It matters not... Having a heart... Being human... It's all irrelevant, completely and utterly insignificant!
You! You matter not... Nor does anything in this world! Gah! Argh, argh! None of it matters to me!
Heh... Heh...
...Fools. Time to die.
We're... We're safe?
It seems this young lady aided in our escape. You have my sincere gratitude, dear madame.
The flowers here bloom in such peaceful silence. I imagine you would not have invited anyone here, were it not an emergency.

dialogue.sit: Huh, talk about a good judge of character...

dialogue.t: Oh? I take it that means you've been here before, then? In that case, I count myself fortunate to be your associate.
Columbinaaaa... What did you do that for!?!?
I studied his abilities inside-out... Equipped Pulonia with comprehensive countermeasures... We were going to settle the score...!
But he still broke through, did he not?
What, you expect a battle to be completely one-sided!?
I just... didn't expect him to have no sense of honor, whatsoever! Pulonia would have been fine in a head-on clash, but battles just... get chaotic...
Oh... So you actually thought you could win.

Have you been taking care of yourself lately? Your calculations seem to have deviated quite seriously. Perhaps you could try sleeping and rising earlier, or you could adopt my previous recommendation and—
Hey, listen here, Columbina! I tolerated your nonsense previously because we were colleagues.
There's a Fatui warrant out on your head, and don't you forget that. Don't make me fight you right here and now.
Oh, I was just a little concerned about you, that's all... Just like that time when you weren't making any progress with your research, so you went and cooped yourself up all alone...
That was none of your business! And don't you ever drag me out to one of your freaky hovels again!
Come on, Pulonia. We're leaving!
Um... W—Well, anyway, thank you!

dialogue.sit: We would've been in a tight spot without you.
This was quite unexpected.

dialogue.t: I was worried about you, too — not only because the remains of the Eternal Moon Goddess cannot fall into his hands, but also... because you've done much for me yourselves.
And then I... Well, I brought your associate along for the ride, too. But that was as much as I could do.
You're not afraid to speak your mind, miss — I like that. Please, call me Flins. It is my honor to make the acquaintance of one such as yourself.
Still, what do we do now? Rerir's gotten stronger again. At this point, it doesn't seem like we can beat him.
We did block most of the kuuvahki, so I'd say we've put a lid on his plans, for now at least.
But we still don't know what his aims are, and he may continue gathering power... So we must be very careful.
After you left, I could no longer sense his presence...
That means it's safe out there for now, right?
A question, if I may, kind Miss Columbina.
When the cannon's kuuvahki beam was deflected earlier, I saw several bolts of energy streak toward Hiisi Island, only to be blocked. Did you also have a hand in that?
No.
I see... Curious.
Oh, yeah. The cannon veered off course in the end, didn't it? Paimon wonders how Aino and the others are doing. Let's head back and check on them!
In that case, Miss Columbina, I shall not disturb your serenity any longer. Thank you once again for coming to the rescue.
Go now, all of you. Do not worry.

dialogue.sit: Thank you...

dialogue.t: Ugh... Aah...
My strength... still isn't returning...
It seems my time... is running out...

quests.description: You and Flins discover that the cannon’s firing is Rerir’s doing, but his motives remain a mystery. Either way, you are running out of time…

quests.title: Rest Beyond Reach

dialogue.sit: Everyone convenes, recounting what happened to them and sharing what they've learned...

dialogue.t: Fortunately, we were able to minimize the harm. Only a few townspeople were hurt.
But the Rächer of Solnari has now gained a complete form, while we still know nothing about his goals.
It seems we have done something akin to releasing a vicious Qucusaur into the wild.
...I am sorry. Is no one here familiar with Qucusaurs?
P—Paimon knows what you mean, but that analogy seems more than slightly understated...
He said that this world means nothing to him, so it is possible that he doesn't have a reason to fight us at the moment.
If his objective had been revenge alone, we would likely have no recourse.
Is there, uh, still time for me to tender my resignation?
Just kidding, just kidding! Don't worry, Boss, I know there's no running now!
So my cannon, my pride and joy, was a hindrance rather than a help... Gah! You know what? I'm gonna dismantle it, right now!

dialogue.sit: This wasn't your fault, Aino...
Nor was it the cannon's...

dialogue.t: That's right, and it still works on normal Wild Hunt anomalies. Don't let this get you down, Aino!
Flins, we'll need you to attend to the aftermath with the Lightkeepers. Don't worry, I've explained everything to them. You're in the clear.
My thanks — for that, and for everything else I hear you did to help us arrive at the truth.
Had you been willing to show yourself in public more often, you would not have been so easy to isolate, you know.
Heh, point taken. I will give that some thought.
Hmm. I suppose that's one way I'd benefit from replacing Sergeant Major Sousi...
You mean, you're being promoted?

dialogue.sit: He's joking, Paimon...

dialogue.t: Was Paimon the only one who didn't get that?
Well, {NICKNAME}, if you've got a moment, would you like to come with me?
There's a certain gentleman I'd like to send off on his final journey.
This man was like a lighthouse...
Here he lived, as if it were a mere matter of course, and brought light and grace to those around him. But people, once used to illumination, are apt to ignore the lantern's presence.
Slowly, gradually, he came to think as such himself.
"I have achieved too little, I must do better, there is more work to be done..."
Perhaps his end was tragic, but I remain proud of the way in which he illuminated the path for others.
Every shadow born of the light shall remember it.
Poor guy...

dialogue.sit: I once heard the tale of a Lantern Fae.

dialogue.t: Heh. I've heard that one, too.

dialogue.sit: And I'd like to say the same to him.
There's no need to be so fixated on the outcome.

dialogue.t: Is that so?
Well, you're right. It may seem that our efforts were in vain, that Rerir achieved his goals.
But we will pursue him to the last, even if the outcome is not what we wish for.
It is not dissimilar to the role of a Graveyard Keeper...
We do not seek to bring the dead back to life, only to grant them peace.

dialogue.sit: I'm glad to hear that's how you see it.

dialogue.t: Yeah.
Wh—What are you two talking about? Care to explain?

dialogue.sit: Not right now, Paimon. I'll tell you when we get back.

dialogue.t: Okay...
Either way, the Lantern Fae is not playing the leading role in these final rites.
"Light-bearer, with your blood, you have paved the road to glory and justice."
"Even as we hurry on, bruised and battered though we may be, stay awhile and look back upon the world and all its love and hatred."
"Until it closes its eyes in the depths of night, and a lantern lit for you alone flickers softly into life."
Thank you for everything, Sergeant Major Sousi.
Flins? Don't see you coming around here often. Just feel free to take a look. I'm busy right now.
Well, I've come to visit you, Miss Aino. Here — I've brought some snacks from town in their traditional butter flavor. So, where should I leave them...
Shh! ... Ineffa might hear you.
...So, what's the occasion? Are you... gonna to say that the Ratniki will be taking over all Wild Hunt incidents after that hiccup with the cannon?
And criticize a genius like yourself on account of results that none of us could anticipate? We would not be that crass.
If we really did do that, I daresay we shall never again see technological breakthroughs.
Hmph. Sweet-talker...
It gladdens me to have set your heart at ease.
Anyway, what's the matter, exactly?
Well. Could you help me repair this lantern? I did bring it to Nasha Town to get it fixed, but it broke again during our previous battle.
You want a genius like me to go fix a lantern?
Oh, my apologies. Perhaps this request should be better directed to Miss Ineffa, and perhaps the snacks too...
Wh—Wh—Wh... I... I mean, I can totally do this, no problem. Wait right there. I'll be done before you can say "Fix-it!"
Much obliged, then.
And next time this happens to you, make sure to come to me first, you hear?
Krumkake creation complete. Please, enjoy while it's hot.
Thank you for going to the trouble of remembering that, Miss Ineffa. May this taste bear witness to a friendship that will endure forever and a day.
Understood. However, I fear that krumkakes do not keep for that long. A week at most may pass before their taste deteriorates.
Hehe, that's not quite what I meant by... Hmm?
Oh? We appear to have some guests.
Ah, they must have followed the aroma of the krumkake... It's alright, come closer. Ineffa is a friend.
Affirmative. In fact, I can devise a cereal omelette based on individual preferences, before crushing it into servings to share around.
What are they saying?
They... are discussing your address. They wish to go home with you.
Boss, I... Do you remember that thing... that I wanted to ask your opinion about?
On a scale of 1 to 10, how much effort should the Curatorium of Secrets put in if we were to work with others again?
Hehe.
Is that a 1? Isn't that kinda low...
Guess again.
Wait, you mean zero? But wouldn't we just be slapping our brand on the joint venture and calling it a day? Why even team up at that point?
*sigh* ...Jahoda.
What I mean to say is that there is neither an upper nor lower limit.
Huh! That's just like you, Boss, always thinking ahead...
Wait a minute, that's not an answer at all, is it? C'mon, just give me a number, boss, please!
Hmm? What brings you here? Didn't expect to see you around again...
And where have you been, huh? Didn't run away or anything, did ya?
Oh, of course not! I was simply elsewhere discussing business deals.
Indeed, it was all thanks to you that my little store was saved. *sob* I am grateful. So grateful...

dialogue.sit: Okay, okay, you can cut it with the acting now...

dialogue.t: What? Why, I wasn't acting in the slightest!
And didn't I tell you that my prices were reasonable? Ah, but you still turned to that Curatorium of Secrets, or whatever it is they call it.
*sigh* If even regulars such as you abandon ship like this, what can a businesswoman do but take her wares elsewhere...?

dialogue.sit: You're way too wary of the Curatorium...

dialogue.t: And how should I not be, hmm? Running small overseas enterprises is no mean feat — never mind when such formidable competition exists...
Ah, forget it. Fortune and destiny are as one, so there is no use complaining.
It's not as if Nefer did me no favors on account of our common homeland when I first arrived.
If anything is to blame, it is the lack of opportunity to have her owe me in turn, big time!
Now then! Should she ever need anything, you make sure — no, make doubly sure — to inform me first, alright?
"Fix my lantern," he says. Puh-lease! This won't take ten minutes!
If only everyone knew what the heck they were doing...

Take that Hintsa for instance. How in the world do you end up creating an integrated controller for the cannon AND the barrier from random components people ask you to fix!? Ugh, gives me a headache just thinking about it...
I gave him a real earful, and told him to send me regular reports — if he's been working on it lately, I wanna hear about it! *sigh* Y—Yeah, I mean, I know I'm partly at fault too, alright?
Ah, fancy meeting you here, {NICKNAME}. I've decided my lantern has earned itself some thorough maintenance after that rather intense battle.
Thank you for keeping my secrets, despite knowing as much as you do.

dialogue.sit: I didn't have time to ask this before, but...
Why were the Lightkeepers able to detect your lantern?

dialogue.t: Well, because otherwise, I'd get in trouble with the Starshyna. If they couldn't detect my own lantern, I suspect the higher-ups would foist a standard-issue Ratnik lantern on me.
A Ratnik carrying two lanterns — imagine that! It would be an aesthetic transgression of the highest order. Hehe.
Columbina! What are you doing here?
Hmm? Was it not you who recommended such walkabouts to me?
Yeah, but aren't you afraid the Fatui will see you?
Sandrone seems uninterested in my capture, and the others are unlikely to risk making contact at all. They have more troublesome affairs to deal with.

dialogue.sit: (Rerir, if I had to guess... He is a threat to all who live in Nod-Krai.)

dialogue.t: Well, it's good to come out for a walk either way. So, how do you feel? Is Nasha Town to your liking?
Mmm... The flow of kuuvahki is somewhat turbulent, and the people are ill at ease.
However...
However?
Is this where you purchased the dishes you "treated" me to?
(Are you serious? That's what she's concerned about? Berries and Fried Meat?)
Um, well, we can take you to grab a bite if you'd like to. There's all sorts of delicious stuff out here that you won't get to try at home.
...You've been quite subdued. Thorny questions on your mind, perhaps?

dialogue.sit: I'm concerned about Rerir...
Let's talk about the Fatui...
I've been thinking about our spaceship...
I'm good for now.

dialogue.t: I could not gain any insight into his schemes, I fear.
Now that he has donned a shape and form, selling his power short would prove a fatal error.
But that power of his plays host to an obsession that borders on mania.
I cannot say if that fixation is directed at the moons or at something else...
Perhaps understanding the subject of his fixation shall prove key to repelling him in the future...

dialogue.sit: Let's talk about the Fatui...
I've been thinking about our spaceship...
I'm good for now.

dialogue.t: Well, Sandrone's daily routine is highly irregular, while The Doctor often orders people around. As for Arlecchino...
Hmm? Was that not what you were curious about?
Well then. Have you been to that Experimental Design Bureau of theirs? That "weapon" will play a key role in the Tsaritsa's plan. That's what I've heard, anyway.
And what plan is that, precisely? Well, I cannot say I care.

dialogue.sit: I'm concerned about Rerir...
I've been thinking about our spaceship...
I'm good for now.

dialogue.t: ...Interesting.
You've followed me this far. Why not show your face?
Haha, right, right! Right you are. I forgot to introduce myself.
The name's Varka. Knight of Boreas, and Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

quests.description: Rerir used the cannon in Nasha Town to obtain a complete body. The chaos caused by the Wild Hunt is far from over…
